An `<Email>` root renders to email-safe HTML: tables with px widths, inline styles, and Outlook's markup in conditional comments. You write the layout once in elements, and the writer handles the client quirks.

```tsx
import { Column, Email, Text, Row, render } from "@hyper-elements/react";

const { html, text } = await render(
  <Email previewText="Two columns" title="Hi">
    <Row style={{ gap: 16 }}>
      <Column><Text>Left</Text></Column>
      <Column style={{ width: 180 }}><Text style={{ mobile: { fontSize: 14 } }}>Right</Text></Column>
    </Row>
  </Email>
);
```

## The rules it writes by

1. **Right without `<style>`.** Layout at desktop width, colors, fonts, sizes and spacing are inline. The stylesheet only adds phone styles, hiding, hover and client resets. Gmail drops `<style>` for some accounts, and the email still holds its desktop layout.
2. **Widths are decided before writing.** Every table, cell and image gets a px width attribute from the layout resolver. Outlook's Word engine sizes by attributes and ignores the sizes of `div`s.
3. **Tables for layout**, with `role="presentation"`, no spacing and no borders. Spacing is cell padding.
4. **Outlook-only markup only inside `<!--[if mso]>`**, and nothing other clients need inside one.

## What you get

The document is the Unlayer editor's email shell: an XHTML doctype, Office settings for Outlook, `x-apple-disable-message-reformatting`, `X-UA-Compatible`, `-webkit-text-size-adjust`, `color-scheme`, a `border-collapse` reset, and the preview text. The content sits in a full-width table with the window's background, inside a centered table of the content's width. The language, direction and background are also on a `role="article"` wrapper, since Gmail drops `<html>` and `<body>`.

How each element is written:

| Element | In the email |
|-----------|--------------|
| `Section` | A full-width row with its background, its content at the content width inside it |
| `Row` | Each child an inline-block `div`, with an Outlook-only table of the same widths in conditional comments. With `stackOnMobile={false}`, a table row |
| `Column` and other boxes | A one-cell table around the content (Word has no box on a `div` or `p`), its children as table rows |
| Text blocks | The semantic tag with `margin:0`, every text style on it (Outlook doesn't pass styles down through tables), and line heights in px with `mso-line-height-rule: exactly` |
| `Button` | A one-cell table: background, border and corners on the cell, the padding on the link so all of it is clickable, and as the cell's `mso-padding-alt` for Outlook |
| `Image` | An `<img>` with a px `width` attribute, fluid elsewhere (`width:100%` up to its width), its height in proportion when the file's size is known |
| `Divider` | A table with a top border and an empty cell Word can't make taller |
| `List` | A table: an item a row, its marker right-aligned in a cell of the indent's width, with `role="list"` and `"listitem"` |
| `Table` | A data table with fixed layout: column widths in a `colgroup` and on each cell, header rows in `thead` with `th` |
| `Span` | A `<span>`, or `<sup>` and `<sub>` with no line height of their own, so a line keeps its height |
| `Video` | Its thumbnail, linked to the video. An email can't play one |

The Button is a table, not VML: captures of classic Outlook show Word drawing a VML button's label in its own font, wrapped inside the shape's fixed size.

## Rows that stack without media queries

A Row is written "fluid hybrid": each child is an inline-block as wide as its desktop width at most, and 100% otherwise. The children sit side by side where there's room and stack where there isn't, without a media query, so they stack in clients that ignore `<style>` too. Outlook gets a table of the same widths inside conditional comments.

The stylesheet adds the rest for phones: a stacked child goes full width, and your `mobile` styles apply. In an email, phones are below the content width plus 20px, so a 600px email's phone rules apply at 620px and narrower.

## Preview text

`previewText` is shown after the subject in inbox lists, not in the email. It's written as a hidden block at the top of the body, and left out of the plain text.

## Merge tags

A `MergeTag` is written in your sending service's syntax, `{{name}}` by default, in the HTML and the plain text. A link's `href` can be a merge tag too. See [Rendering](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/rendering#merge-tags).

## Fonts

Web fonts in `fonts` are written as `@font-face` rules where classic Outlook doesn't read them, so Outlook draws the next font in the stack. Apple Mail and iOS Mail load web fonts. Gmail and classic Outlook don't. End every stack on a font the client has: `"Inter, Arial, sans-serif"`. See [Styles](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/styles#fonts).

## Size budgets

Gmail clips a message after about 100 KB of HTML, and reads 16 KB of a `<style>`. `@hyper-elements/email-clients`' plugin warns about both when it's passed to `render()` (`email/size`, `email/style-size`).

## Seeing it in the clients

The email client emulator, `renderInEmailClients()` from `@hyper-elements/email-clients`, shows the email as each email client shows it, as HTML files you open in a browser, with what each client changed listed. Nothing is sent or uploaded. See [Email client emulator](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/email-client-emulator).

## What email can't do

`validate()` tells you each of these for your design, with the path; the ones about particular clients come from `@hyper-elements/email-clients`' plugin:

- **Svg.** The Email writer has no inline SVG (Gmail and classic Outlook drop it), so an `Svg` in an email is an error. Use an `Image` of it, a PNG.
- **Layer.** An email draws one shape of it: an Image as wide as the Layer, with one child over it. The image is the cell's background, with VML for Outlook.
- **`justifyContent: "space-between"`.** The children start at the left.
- **Rounded corners and letter spacing in classic Outlook.** Corners are square, and letter spacing is normal. The plugin notes it (`email/outlook-degraded`).
- **A Vimeo video's thumbnail.** It can't be found without the network, so give the `Video` a `thumbnail`.
- **An Image without its file's size.** Outlook shows it at the file's size, however wide that is. Give `src` its `width` and `height`.

There are no dark-mode styles yet. The head declares `color-scheme` as light.

## How it's checked

- Unit tests of each element's markup.
- A hostile-input test: user text, links and font URLs with markup in them add no element or attribute, including inside Outlook's comments.
- Chromium tests that every box is as wide as the layout says on desktop, with and without the stylesheet, that Rows stack on phones either way, that hover, fonts and superscripts work, and that Row widths match the page in every min, max and gap case.
- Checks against a model of classic Outlook's layout, built from captures of real Outlook, at 96 and 192 DPI.

> **Warning:** Chromium and a model of Outlook aren't email clients. The output hasn't been checked in real email clients yet, and button padding through `mso-padding-alt` hasn't been measured in real Outlook. Send tests to the clients your users have before you rely on a layout.

The layout doesn't measure text, either. A box with less room than its words needs looks different in email, where the table cell widens to its longest word, than on a page. See [Layout](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/layout#how-widths-are-worked-out).

---

# Page

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/outputs/page

A `<Page>` root renders to a responsive web page: one HTML element per element, semantic tags, inline styles and flexbox. Use it for the web version of an email, a receipt behind a login, or a landing page you generate on the server.

```tsx
import { Button, Column, Heading, Page, Text, Row, render } from "@hyper-elements/react";

const { html } = await render(
  <Page title="Pricing" description="Plans for teams of every size" width={960}>
    <Heading>Pricing</Heading>
    <Row style={{ gap: 16 }}>
      <Column>
        <Text hidden={{ mobile: true }}>Compare every plan side by side.</Text>
      </Column>
      <Column>
        <Button href="/buy" style={{ hover: { backgroundColor: "#374151" } }}>Buy</Button>
      </Column>
    </Row>
  </Page>,
  { pretty: true }
);
```

## What you get

The HTML above, shortened where it says `…`:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <title>Pricing</title>
    <meta name="description" content="Plans for teams of every size">
    <style>.emw6dn:hover{background-color:#374151!important}@media (max-width: 480px){…}</style>
  </head>
  <body style="margin:0">
    <main style="max-width:960px;margin:0 auto;display:flex;flex-direction:column;…">
      <h1 style="margin:0;font-size:32px;font-weight:700;line-height:1.25">Pricing</h1>
      <div class="emfqa6" style="display:flex;gap:16px">…</div>
    </main>
  </body>
</html>
```

- **Semantic tags**: `main`, `section`, `h1` to `h6`, `p`, `ul` and `ol`, `table`, `a`, `img`.
- **Styles inline**, with flexbox for Rows and stacks.
- **A small stylesheet** for what inline styles can't say: phone styles, hiding, hover, and a Row stacking on phones. Its classes are short and named after their rule, so the same design always gets the same classes.
- **No client-side JavaScript** and no React hydration markers. The page is plain HTML.

The content is centered and as wide as the Page's `width` at most, 1200px by default. A `Section`'s background spans the window, with its content at that width. On phones, at 480px and narrower, Rows stack and `mobile` styles apply.

A `Video` is its player on a page: YouTube's or Vimeo's embed, in a 16:9 box. Web fonts in `fonts` are `@font-face` rules with `font-display: swap`.

## Embed it in your own page

`render()` also returns the document in parts, so you can put the output inside a page of your own, a Next.js route or a CMS layout. With the `InvoiceContent` from [Designs](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/designs#share-content-between-roots):

```tsx
import { Page, render } from "@hyper-elements/react";

const { head, body, bodyStyle } = await render(<Page title="Receipt"><InvoiceContent invoice={invoice} /></Page>, { classPrefix: "receipt-" });
```

| Part | What it is |
|------|------------|
| `head` | What goes in `<head>`: meta tags, the title, the stylesheet |
| `body` | What goes in `<body>`: the `<main>` and everything in it |
| `bodyStyle` | The body's own style, such as `margin:0;background-color:#fafafa` for a Page with a background |

`classPrefix` sets what every class in the stylesheet starts with (`e` by default), so the output's rules don't collide with the CSS already on your page. With `classPrefix: "receipt-"`, a class looks like `receipt-mw6dn`.

> **Tip:** Embedding and the plain `html` come from the same render, so a page you embed and the one you serve on its own are the same markup.

## Page, Document and Canvas

A `Document` renders to print HTML with the same page writer, plus a CSS `@page` size, page breaks and one box per page. A `Canvas` renders to HTML to look at, at its fixed size. See [PDF](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/outputs/pdf) and [Image](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/outputs/image).

## Limits

- The layout gives every box a width in px without measuring text. A box with less room than its words needs overflows on a page. See [Layout](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/layout#how-widths-are-worked-out).
- `validate()` reports what a page can't show as asked (`web/unsupported`).

---

# PDF

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/outputs/pdf

A `<Document>` root lays its content out on pages of a fixed size, with a header and a footer on each. `render()` writes it as print-ready HTML, and `renderPdf()` from `@hyper-elements/react/pdf` writes it as a PDF, on your server, with no headless Chrome.

```tsx
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { Document, Heading, Image, PageBreak, PageFooter, PageHeader, PageNumber, Text, Table, TableCell, TableRow } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import { renderPdf } from "@hyper-elements/react/pdf";

const Invoice = () => (
  <Document size="A4" margin={48} title="Invoice 2705" style={{ fontFamily: "Inter, sans-serif", gap: 16 }}>
    <PageHeader style={{ padding: [0, 0, 16, 0] }}>
      <Image src={{ src: "https://cdn.acme.com/logo.png", width: 240, height: 80 }} alt="Acme" style={{ width: 120 }} />
    </PageHeader>
    <Heading level={1}>Invoice 2705</Heading>
    <Text>Thank you for your order.</Text>
    <Table style={{ cellPadding: [8, 0], rowBorder: "1px solid #e4e4e7" }}>
      <TableRow header>
        <TableCell>Item</TableCell>
        <TableCell style={{ textAlign: "right" }}>Price</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
      <TableRow>
        <TableCell>Linen shirt</TableCell>
        <TableCell style={{ textAlign: "right" }}>$48.00</TableCell>
      </TableRow>
    </Table>
    <PageBreak />
    <Heading level={2}>Terms</Heading>
    <Text>Payment is due in 30 days.</Text>
    <PageFooter>
      <Text style={{ fontSize: 10, textAlign: "right" }}>
        Page <PageNumber /> of <PageNumber total />
      </Text>
    </PageFooter>
  </Document>
);

const { pdf, diagnostics } = await renderPdf(<Invoice />, {
  fonts: [
    { family: "Inter", src: await readFile("fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf") },
    { family: "Inter", src: await readFile("fonts/Inter-Bold.ttf"), weight: 700 },
  ],
  images: { "https://cdn.acme.com/logo.png": await readFile("images/logo.png") },
});
for (const { code, message } of diagnostics) console.warn(code, message);
await writeFile("invoice.pdf", pdf);
```

## Install

```bash
npm install @hyper-elements/react @react-pdf/renderer react react-dom
```

| Peer dependency | Version | Why |
|-----------------|---------|-----|
| `@react-pdf/renderer` | `^4.9.0` (optional: only for `/pdf`) | Draws the pages |
| `react`, `react-dom` | `>=18` | |

`/pdf` is an entry of `@hyper-elements/react`. Its engine is an optional peer dependency, so a project that doesn't import `/pdf` installs nothing for it, and the main entry never loads it.

It runs in Node.js only. If it loads a second copy of `@hyper-elements/react` that lays designs out in another version, `renderPdf()` throws an `ElementsError` (`pdf/version`) rather than drawing the design wrong.

## The Document

| Prop | Takes | Default |
|------|-------|---------|
| `size` | `"A3"`, `"A4"`, `"A5"`, `"Letter"`, `"Legal"`, `"Tabloid"` | `"A4"` |
| `orientation` | `"portrait"`, `"landscape"` | `"portrait"` |
| `margin` | Insets around each page's content, its header and footer too, in px at 96 to the inch | 48 on every side |
| `title`, `lang`, `dir`, `fonts` | As on every root | |

A Document's width comes from its size and margin: an A4 page with 48px margins has 698px of content. It has no phone layout, so `mobile` styles are an error in one.

### Pages

The content goes on pages in one of two ways:

- **Runs split by [`PageBreak`](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/pagebreak).** What follows a `PageBreak` starts the next page.
- **[`Document.Page`](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/document-page)s.** Each one is a page, its children stacked inside the Document's margins.

```tsx
<Document size="Letter" orientation="landscape">
  <Document.Page style={{ gap: 16 }}>
    <Heading>Q3 report</Heading>
    <Text>Revenue grew 12%.</Text>
  </Document.Page>
  <Document.Page style={{ gap: 16 }}>
    <Heading level={2}>Details</Heading>
  </Document.Page>
</Document>
```

### Header, footer and page numbers

One [`PageHeader`](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/pageheader) and one [`PageFooter`](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/pagefooter) are drawn on every page, inside its margins. A second of either is an error. A [`PageNumber`](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/pagenumber) in their text, or anywhere in the Document's text, is the number of the page it's on, and `<PageNumber total />` is how many pages there are.

A table row with `footer` ends the table.

## Print HTML

`render()` writes a Document as print HTML: a box of the paper's size for each page, with the header and footer in each, and a CSS `@page` rule for the paper's size and orientation, with no page margin.

```tsx
import { render } from "@hyper-elements/react";

const { html } = await render(<Invoice />);
```

Open it in a browser to look at the pages, or print it. If you print it to PDF with Playwright, pass `preferCSSPageSize: true` and `printBackground: true` to `page.pdf()`, and set the margin on the Document: a `margin` passed to `page.pdf()` changes nothing, since each page draws its own.

## renderPdf()

`renderPdf(element, options)` returns `{ pdf, diagnostics }`: the file's bytes, and the warnings and notes. Errors reject with an `ElementsError` listing them. Its pages, header, footer and page numbers are the print HTML's, laid out at the same widths.

The same design writes the same bytes. The `date` option is when the PDF says it was made: a fixed date by default, which is what keeps the bytes the same. Pass `new Date()` if you want the real one.

| Option | What it takes |
|--------|---------------|
| `fonts` | Font files, by family (below) |
| `images` | Image files, by URL (below) |
| `date` | When the PDF says it was made, a fixed date by default |

### Fonts and images

Nothing is fetched. Give each file the design needs, as bytes:

- **Fonts** in `fonts`: `{ family, src, weight?, style? }`, one entry per file. `src` is a TTF, OTF or WOFF file's bytes. `family` is the name your `fontFamily` stacks use. The files in a Document's `fonts` prop are for its HTML: `renderPdf()` doesn't load them, `data:` URIs included.
- **Images** in `images`, by the URL the design gives them (`{ "https://…/logo.png": bytes }`), or as `data:` URIs in the design. A PDF draws PNG and JPEG.

Text whose `fontFamily` has no file given is drawn in a standard PDF font: Helvetica, Times or Courier, whichever is closest. Those draw Western European characters only. For any other script, give a font file that has it.

A `Video` shows its thumbnail where its file is given (its own, or a YouTube video's by the URL `img.youtube.com/vi/<id>/0.jpg`), and otherwise its title, linked to the video.

### Diagnostics

| Code | Severity | When |
|------|----------|------|
| `pdf/root` | error | The design isn't a Document |
| `pdf/version` | error | A second copy of `@hyper-elements/react` lays the design out in another version |
| `pdf/image` | error | An image isn't given, or its file isn't a PNG or JPEG |
| `pdf/image` | warning | An image is SVG: its alt text is shown in its box |
| `pdf/font` | warning | A font in the Document's `fonts` isn't given, a file given is WOFF2, or text in a standard PDF font has characters it can't draw |
| `pdf/font-weight` | warning | Text in a weight or style of a family that isn't given. It's drawn in the nearest file given |
| `pdf/unsupported` | warning | What a PDF can't show that the HTML can: a hover, a Video's player, an `Html` block's markup (its plain text is drawn), a line too wide to wrap (it goes past the edge) |
| `document/overflow` | warning | A page's content looks taller than the page. An estimate: text isn't measured yet |

`validate()` from `@hyper-elements/react` reports `pdf/unsupported` and `document/overflow` without rendering. The font and image checks need the files, so only `renderPdf()` makes them.

## Limits

- **Nothing flows from one page to the next.** Content taller than its page is cut off, and you get `document/overflow`. Split it with a `PageBreak` or into `Document.Page`s, and test with your longest real data.
- **WOFF2 isn't drawn.** react-pdf would embed its letters blank. Give TTF, OTF or WOFF.
- **SVG images aren't drawn.** Give a PNG or JPEG. An `Svg` element is drawn as vectors.
- **The standard PDF fonts draw Western European characters only.** Whether a font file you give has every character isn't checked.
- **No hover and no video player.** A Button shows its own colors, a Video its thumbnail or title.

---

# Image

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/outputs/image

A `<Canvas>` root is an image of a fixed size. `renderImage()` from `@hyper-elements/react/image` writes it as a PNG or an SVG, on your server, with Satori and resvg. No browser, no screenshot service, no network.

```tsx
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { Canvas, Circle, Heading, Image, Text, Row, Svg } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import { renderImage } from "@hyper-elements/react/image";

function PostCard({ title, author }: { title: string; author: string }) {
  return (
    <Canvas width={1200} height={630} style={{ backgroundColor: "#0f172a", padding: 64, gap: 24, color: "#ffffff", fontFamily: "Inter, sans-serif", justifyContent: "space-between" }}>
      <Image src={{ src: "https://example.com/logo.png", width: 240, height: 80 }} alt="Acme" style={{ width: 120 }} />
      <Heading level={1} style={{ fontSize: 64 }}>{title}</Heading>
      <Row style={{ gap: 16, alignItems: "center" }}>
        <Svg width={40} height={40} style={{ flex: "none" }}>
          <Circle cx={20} cy={20} r={20} style={{ fill: "#38bdf8" }} />
        </Svg>
        <Text style={{ fontSize: 28, color: "#cbd5e1" }}>{author}</Text>
      </Row>
    </Canvas>
  );
}

const { image, width, height, diagnostics } = await renderImage(<PostCard title="Launch week" author="Ada Lovelace" />, {
  fonts: [
    { family: "Inter", src: await readFile("fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf") },
    { family: "Inter", src: await readFile("fonts/Inter-Bold.ttf"), weight: 700 },
  ],
  images: { "https://example.com/logo.png": await readFile("images/logo.png") },
});
await writeFile("card.png", image);
```

Use it for social cards, Open Graph images, banners, or any image you'd otherwise build in a design tool and export by hand. Pass a different `title` and you have a card per blog post.

## Install

```bash
npm install @hyper-elements/react satori@^0.33.5 @resvg/resvg-js react react-dom
```

Give satori's range as above. pnpm and yarn otherwise add satori's newest version, outside the range `/image` is built for, with only a warning, and it draws some Canvases wrong.

| Peer dependency | Version | Why |
|-----------------|---------|-----|
| `satori` | `^0.33.5` (optional: only for `/image`) | Lays out the Canvas and draws its text as paths, as SVG |
| `@resvg/resvg-js` | `^2.6.2` (optional: only for `/image`) | Draws that SVG as a PNG |
| `react`, `react-dom` | `>=18` | |

`/image` is an entry of `@hyper-elements/react`. Its engines are optional peer dependencies, so a project that doesn't import `/image` installs nothing for them, and the main entry never loads them.

It runs in Node.js only. If it loads a second copy of `@hyper-elements/react` that lays designs out in another version, `renderImage()` throws an `ElementsError` (`image/version`) rather than drawing the design wrong.

> **Note:** Satori runs WebAssembly, which a Content-Security-Policy without `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` blocks. That's one reason image output is its own entry, `@hyper-elements/react/image`, which the main entry never loads.

In Next.js, list both engines in `next.config.ts`, so Next.js loads them from `node_modules` instead of bundling them: resvg is a native addon, and Satori reads a WebAssembly file when it runs. Without it, `next build` fails on resvg, and a route that draws an image fails on Satori's file.

```ts
// next.config.ts
export default { serverExternalPackages: ["@resvg/resvg-js", "satori"] };
```

Satori lays out all of a Canvas's text, the part that's cut off too, so a very long text takes time and memory in proportion: about 1 GB for a 100,000-character title. Limit the length of text that comes from users to what the Canvas can show.

## The Canvas

| Prop | What it does | Default |
|------|--------------|---------|
| `width` | The image's width in px | 1200 |
| `height` | The image's height in px. What's past it is cut | 630 |
| `title`, `lang`, `dir`, `fonts` | As on every root | |

Its content is laid out as on a page, with no phone layout. Beside the text styles, `backgroundColor`, `gap` and `alignItems`, a Canvas's `style` takes `padding` and `justifyContent`, so you can push content to the bottom or spread it out (`"space-between"`).

`render()` writes a Canvas as HTML too, to look at in a browser while you design it.

## renderImage()

`renderImage(element, options)` returns `{ image, width, height, diagnostics }`: the file's bytes, its size in pixels, and the warnings and notes. Errors reject with an `ElementsError` listing them. The same design writes the same bytes.

| Option | What it takes |
|--------|---------------|
| `fonts` | Font files, by family (below) |
| `images` | Image files, by URL (below) |
| `format` | `"png"` (the default) or `"svg"`. An SVG's text is drawn as paths, so it shows without the fonts |
| `scale` | Pixels per px of a PNG: 2 for a phone's screen. At 2, a 1200 by 630 Canvas is 2400 by 1260 |

```tsx
const { image } = await renderImage(<PostCard title="Launch week" author="Ada Lovelace" />, { fonts, images, format: "svg" });
await writeFile("card.svg", image);
```

### Fonts and images

Nothing is fetched. Give each file the design needs, as bytes:

- **Fonts** in `fonts`: `{ family, src, weight?, style? }`, one entry per file. `src` is a TTF, OTF or WOFF file's bytes, and `family` is the name your `fontFamily` stacks use. A Canvas's own `fonts` given as `data:` URIs are drawn too. Ones given by URL aren't loaded.
- **Images** in `images`, by the URL the design gives them (`{ "https://…/photo.png": bytes }`), or as `data:` URIs in the design: PNG, JPEG, GIF or SVG.

An image with text needs at least one font. Text whose `fontFamily` has no file given is drawn in the first font given.

### Diagnostics

| Code | Severity | When |
|------|----------|------|
| `image/root` | error | The design isn't a Canvas |
| `image/version` | error | A second copy of `@hyper-elements/react` lays the design out in another version |
| `image/font` | error | The Canvas has text and no font is given |
| `image/font` | warning | A font in the Canvas's `fonts` isn't given, or a file given is WOFF2 |
| `image/font-weight` | warning | Text in a weight or style of a family that isn't given. It's drawn in the nearest file given |
| `image/image` | error | An image isn't given, or its file isn't a PNG, JPEG, GIF or SVG |
| `image/unsupported` | warning | What an image can't show that the HTML can: a hover, a Video's player, an `Html` block's markup (its plain text is drawn), a line too wide to wrap (it goes past the edge) |
| `canvas/overflow` | warning | The content looks taller than the Canvas. An estimate: text isn't measured yet |

`validate()` from `@hyper-elements/react` reports `image/unsupported` and `canvas/overflow` without rendering. The font and image checks need the files, so only `renderImage()` makes them.

## Fitting text, measuring and strict

A Heading or a Text in a Canvas takes `fit={{ sizes, maxLines }}`: `renderImage()` measures it with the fonts given and draws the largest size at which its lines, its widest piece that can't break (a word, or words a no-break space holds together; Chinese and Japanese text breaks between its characters) and any fixed-height box around it fit, or fails with `image/fit` naming the lines and roughly what to cut. Several fitted nodes are sized in document order, each tried with the ones after it at their smallest size. `sizes` is a list of px sizes or `{ min, max, step }`; with only `maxLines` it checks the size the text has. The HTML preview draws the largest size.

`layoutImage(design, { fonts, images, scale, strict })` measures without drawing: each block's box, each fitted node's sizes and the one chosen, and the characters no font covers. `strict: true` makes a missing font, weight or character, and content past the Canvas, errors; a template's design is drawn strict.

## Limits

- **WOFF2 isn't drawn.** Satori reads TTF, OTF and WOFF. Give one of those.
- **Text is drawn only in the fonts you give.** A character none of them has comes out as an empty box. Give a font that has it.
- **What doesn't fit is cut off** at the Canvas's edges. Text isn't measured before layout, so check long titles: `canvas/overflow` is an estimate.
- **No hover and no video.** A Button shows its own colors, a Video its title.

---

# Templates

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates

A template is written once, by your team: the brand's parts are locked, and a few parts are left open. People and
agents make designs from it by filling the open parts, and the template checks each one before anything is drawn. It's
`@hyper-elements/react/template`, and it runs wherever a design does: no service, account or engine of its own.

<div class="output-gallery">
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/orbit-square.png" title="Open the square launch graphic at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/orbit-square.png" width="1080" height="1080" alt="The square launch graphic: Orbit's logo, the launch date, the headline and three features, and the product screenshot in a window over a panel of bold, colorful shapes"></a><figcaption>square, 1080×1080</figcaption></figure>
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/orbit-landscape.png" title="Open the landscape launch graphic at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/orbit-landscape.png" width="1200" height="630" alt="The landscape launch graphic: the same copy on the left, and on the right the product screenshot in its window over the same shapes"></a><figcaption>landscape, 1200×630</figcaption></figure>
</div>

Both images came from one template and one set of values. [Template examples](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/examples) builds
that template step by step, and three more: an email with a locked header and footer around an open body, a
newsletter whose body takes only what the brand allows, and an invoice filled from data. Every option is in the
reference:

- [Values: fields, images and formats](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields)
- [Content: slots and blocks](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots)
- [Rules, checks and diagnostics](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/rules)
- [Templates in the command line](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/cli)

## What a template is

<figure class="diagram"><a href="/generated/templates-guide/parts.svg" title="Open the diagram at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/parts.svg" width="884" height="486" alt="The square launch graphic with its parts outlined. The logo is locked. The headline, the three features, the launch date, the screenshot and the artwork are open fields. Everything else (layout, colors, fonts, sizes) is locked."></a></figure>

- **Locked parts** are the template's: the logo, the layout of each format, the colors and the fonts. No value can
  change them.
- **Open parts** are what a design gives. Here they're six **fields**, each with its limits: the five outlined, and
  the language, which has nothing to outline. A template can also open **blocks** (approved section types, picked and
  ordered as data) and **slots** (JSX someone writes, with only the elements and styles the template allows).
- **Rules over the result** are checked on the finished design: here, that nothing runs past the Canvas, every
  character has a font, and the headline fits.

A **design** is one finished piece: this launch's graphic, this month's newsletter. Any Email, Page, Document or
Canvas is a design. One made from a template is checked by it.

## How an agent sees a template

An agent gets the same template you do, read as what it may change and what it may not. Here is an event invitation
with a divider between the two: on the left the email as you see it, on the right as an agent sees it. Green is open,
each field labeled with its limits: the event's name (up to 60 characters), the tagline (20 to 120), the date, the
venue and the hours (no year), and the day's schedule (up to eight rows, or none, each up to 100 characters).
Red is locked: the logo, the layout and the footer.

<div class="output-gallery single">
<figure><a href="/img/templates/agent-view.webp" title="Open the event invitation as you see it and as an agent sees it at full size"><img src="/img/templates/agent-view.webp" width="736" height="948" loading="lazy" alt="An event invitation split by a divider. The left part is the email as you see it. The right part is the same email as an agent sees it: the event name, tagline, date, venue, hours and each schedule line in green, each labeled Allowed to change with its limits, and the header and footer in red, labeled Locked."></a><figcaption>The event invitation template, as you see it and as an agent sees it</figcaption></figure>
</div>

Every template in the [template gallery](https://www.hyperelements.dev/templates) opens with this view: emails, pages, PDFs and images. Drag the divider to compare
the two.

## The parts, one at a time

A template has six kinds of part. Four hold what a design gives (a field, an image field, blocks, a slot), one sets
the sizes it's made in (formats), and one checks the result (rules):

<div class="concept-grid">
<a class="concept" href="/docs/templates/fields#fields"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/concept-field.svg" width="600" height="400" loading="lazy" alt="The launch graphic with only its headline lit and outlined: a field"><strong>Field</strong><span>One typed value a design gives: text, a date, a number, a choice, a list.</span></a>
<a class="concept" href="/docs/templates/fields#image-limits"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/concept-image.svg" width="600" height="400" loading="lazy" alt="A product screenshot at 1.6 to 1 marked taken, and a banner at 4 to 1 marked refused: an image field's rules"><strong>Image field</strong><span>A picture, with limits on its shape, size and type.</span></a>
<a class="concept" href="/docs/templates/fields#formats-and-the-example"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/concept-format.svg" width="600" height="400" loading="lazy" alt="The launch graphic as a square image and as a landscape image: two formats"><strong>Format</strong><span>The same design at another size, from the same values.</span></a>
<a class="concept" href="/docs/templates/slots#slots"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/concept-slot.svg" width="600" height="400" loading="lazy" alt="An email with only its body lit and outlined: a slot"><strong>Slot</strong><span>A region someone writes freely, as JSX, inside limits the template sets.</span></a>
<a class="concept" href="/docs/templates/slots#blocks"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/concept-blocks.svg" width="600" height="400" loading="lazy" alt="Two emails made of the same three section types, story, quote and button, in different orders: blocks"><strong>Blocks</strong><span>Approved sections, picked and ordered as data.</span></a>
<a class="concept" href="/docs/templates/rules#rules-over-the-result"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/concept-rule.svg" width="600" height="400" loading="lazy" alt="An email whose button links to another company's site, the button outlined in red and the email refused: a rule"><strong>Rule</strong><span>Something that must hold on the finished design, whatever filled it.</span></a>
</div>

## Which one do I need?

| You want | Use | Whoever fills it gives |
|----------|-----|------------------------|
| A value to change: a headline, a date, a price | A [field](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields#fields) | Data |
| A picture to change, kept to a shape and size | An [image field](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields#image-limits) | An image file |
| The same design at several sizes | [Formats](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields#formats-and-the-example) | Nothing more: the same values |
| Sections chosen from a set you approve | [Blocks](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots#blocks) | Data: each section's type and its values |
| Content someone writes, in your look or freely | A [slot](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots#slots) | JSX |
| Something that's always true of the result | A [rule](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/rules#rules-over-the-result) | Nothing: the template checks it |

Start with fields. Reach for blocks when the sections vary, and for a slot only when the content can't be listed ahead
of time: the more a template leaves open, the more its rules have to carry.

All four open parts are declared the same way, in the template's `fields`. Blocks and slots are listed apart here
because what they hold is content, not one value.

## What each root takes

Every part works in an Email, a Page, a Document and a Canvas, except formats. What differs is how much the template
can check:

| Part | Email | Page | Document | Canvas |
|------|-------|------|----------|--------|
| Field | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Image field | Yes. Its shape, size and type are checked. Its file is read only where it sits beside the design, not at a URL | Yes, as in an Email | Yes. The command line reads its file | Yes, and measured where it's drawn: an image that would be upscaled is refused |
| Format | Not needed: one width, which phone styles adapt | Not needed: it fits the window | Page sizes: A4, Letter | Image sizes: square, landscape |
| Slot, blocks | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Rules | Links, layout overflow, and lint's rules for an email: an unsubscribe link, preview text, contrast, alternate text | Links, layout overflow, and lint's rules for a page: a title, headings in order, contrast, alternate text | Links, layout and page overflow | Links, and what measuring decides: fitted text, overflow, a font for every character |

## What you need

| To | Install |
|----|---------|
| Write templates and designs | `@hyper-elements/react`, with `react` and `react-dom`. Templates are its `/template` entry |
| Run the commands on these pages | `@hyper-elements/cli`, which gives `npx hyper-elements` |
| Require lint's rules in a template | `@hyper-elements/lint` |
| Have email client checks reported | `@hyper-elements/email-clients` |
| Draw a Canvas as an image | `satori` and `@resvg/resvg-js` |
| Draw a Document as a PDF | `@react-pdf/renderer` |

```bash
npm i @hyper-elements/react react react-dom
npm i -D @hyper-elements/cli
```

## How it's used

1. **Write the template** once: `template({ … })`, with its fields, its rules and a `render` that builds the design.
2. **Make a design** from it: a values file (the design as JSON, which `design new` writes), or TSX with the template
   as its root.
3. **Check it.** The template checks the values, the design they build, and what can only be known by measuring it.
4. **Render it.** One output per format, and nothing for a design that fails.

```bash
npx hyper-elements design new templates/launch-graphic.tsx -o designs/orbit.values.json \
  --values brief.json --set screenshot=@designs/art/screenshot.png --set artwork=@designs/art/shapes.png
npx hyper-elements check designs/orbit.values.json
npx hyper-elements render designs/orbit.values.json
```

[Template examples](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/examples) runs each step on four templates, with what every command
wrote and what each template refuses, and does the same [from code](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/examples#the-same-from-code).

## What template() takes

A template is a module whose default export is `template({ … })`:

| Key | What it is |
|-----|------------|
| `id` | A namespace, a dot and a capitalized name: `acme.LaunchGraphic` |
| `version` | Semver. A values file records the version it was made with. Raise it when the template changes: an older file is read again, and migrated across a major version |
| `label`, `guidance` | Its name for people, and advice in plain English for whoever fills it. Guidance is never enforced: it's listed for a person to judge |
| `root` | What it makes: `"Email"`, `"Page"`, `"Document"` or `"Canvas"` |
| `formats` | Its named sizes, for a Canvas or a Document. See [formats](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields#formats-and-the-example) |
| `fields` | What's open: [values and images](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields), [blocks and slots](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots) |
| `rules` | What must hold on the finished design. See [rules](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/rules#rules-over-the-result) |
| `example` | A full set of values. Required: it's checked with the template, and it's what whoever fills the template is shown |
| `render(values, { format })` | Builds the design from the values. Whatever it writes that isn't a field is locked |
| `migrate` | For each major version, how an older values file's values become this one's. See [values as data](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields#values-as-data) |

A simple template can instead be written as the design itself, with its open parts marked:
[annotated templates](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots#annotated-templates).

## Keeping templates trusted

A template guarantees what it checks, not who may edit it: a process that can write the template's file can change
it. Two things follow.

- **Protect the templates.** Commit them, review changes to them (with CODEOWNERS, for example), and don't give
  whatever fills them write access to the templates folder.
- **Know which designs are code.** A values file is data: nothing in it runs, so it's the form to take from an agent
  or anyone unreviewed. A TSX design, and a slot stored as a module, are code that runs before the template checks
  anything. Review those as you review any code.

[Templates in the command line](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/cli#trusted-templates) shows how to list the templates a project
trusts, and what `--require-template` does and doesn't guarantee.

---

# Template examples

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/examples

Four templates, each with a picture of what's locked and what's open. All are real: the pictures and the output are
what the commands on this page wrote. [Templates](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates) says what a template is and
[what to install](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates#what-you-need).

The launch graphic is the fullest, and walks through every command. For the shortest template, start with the
[email](#an-email-with-a-locked-header-and-footer).

| Template | Its root | Locked | Open |
|----------|----------|--------|------|
| [Launch graphic](#a-launch-graphic-in-two-sizes) | Canvas | The logo, each size's layout, the colors and the fonts | Six fields: a headline, three features, a date, a language and two pictures |
| [Orbit email](#an-email-with-a-locked-header-and-footer) | Email | The header, the footer and its unsubscribe link | The body: any elements, written as JSX |
| [Newsletter](#a-newsletter-with-a-limited-body) | Email | The header, the footer, the brand's look | A subject, and a body of five kinds of element, with no styles of its own |
| [Orbit invoice](#an-invoice-filled-from-data) | Document | The letterhead, the table, the total, the footer on every page | The customer, the number, the dates, the lines, a note: all data |

The examples are one project. Its templates are in `templates/`, its designs in `designs/`, and its `package.json`
lists the templates it trusts, so no design can name another one
([trusted templates](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/cli#trusted-templates)):

```json
{ "hyperElements": { "templates": ["templates/**"] } }
```

## A launch graphic in two sizes

<div class="output-gallery">
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/orbit-square.png" title="Open the square launch graphic at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/orbit-square.png" width="1080" height="1080" alt="The square launch graphic: Orbit's logo, the launch date, the headline and three features, and the product screenshot in a window over a panel of bold, colorful shapes"></a><figcaption>square, 1080×1080</figcaption></figure>
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/orbit-landscape.png" title="Open the landscape launch graphic at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/orbit-landscape.png" width="1200" height="630" alt="The landscape launch graphic: the same copy on the left, and on the right the product screenshot in its window over the same shapes"></a><figcaption>landscape, 1200×630</figcaption></figure>
</div>

<figure class="diagram"><a href="/generated/templates-guide/parts.svg" title="Open the diagram at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/parts.svg" width="884" height="486" alt="The square launch graphic with its parts outlined. The logo is locked. The headline, the three features, the launch date, the screenshot and the artwork are open fields. Everything else (layout, colors, fonts, sizes) is locked."></a></figure>

- **Locked:** the logo, each size's layout, the colors and the fonts. No value can change them.
- **Open:** six fields, each with its limits: the headline, three features, a date, a language and two pictures.
- **Still checked:** the finished image. Nothing runs past the Canvas, every character has a font, and the headline fits.
- **Formats:** square and landscape. One set of values renders as both.

### Write the template

A template is `template({ … })`: an id and a version, its formats, its fields, an example, and a `render` that builds
the design from the values. The fields say what's open, each with its limits:

```tsx
// from templates/launch-graphic.tsx
fields: {
  headline: prop.text({ label: "Headline", required: true, maxLength: 90 }),
  features: prop.list(prop.text({ label: "Feature", maxLength: 40 }), { label: "Features", required: true, min: 3, max: 3 }),
  launchDate: prop.date({ label: "Launch date", required: true }),
  locale: prop.choice(["en-US", "de-DE"], { label: "Language", default: "en-US" }),
  screenshot: field.image({ label: "Product screenshot", required: true, fit: "contain", aspect: { min: 1.2, max: 2 }, minWidth: 1000, accepts: ["png"] }),
  artwork: field.image({ label: "Artwork", required: true, fit: "cover", maxCrop: 0.6, accepts: ["png"], guidance: "Bold flat shapes in the brand's colors. No text, logos or people." }),
},
```

`render` gets the values and the format's name. Whatever it writes that isn't a field is fixed. A node says which
field it shows with `field="…"`, which is how the template's checks find it. The headline is
[fitted text](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields#fitted-text): drawn at the largest of its sizes that takes three lines or
fewer. What's under it follows it.

```tsx
// from templates/launch-graphic.tsx
<Heading field="headline" level={1} fit={{ sizes: [...f.headline], maxLines: 3 }} style={{ color: INK, lineHeight: 1.06, letterSpacing: -1.5 }}>
  {v.headline}
</Heading>
```

The rules over the result are one line. `require.core` names checks of Elements' own, by their codes. Requiring one
means a design doesn't pass until that check has run and found nothing. These three need the image **measured**:
laid out with its real fonts, which the command line does when it checks a design, and `renderImage()` when it draws
one. So no design passes on its values alone:

```tsx
// from templates/launch-graphic.tsx
rules: { require: { core: ["image/overflow", "image/glyph", "image/fit"] } },
```

<details>
<summary>The whole template: <code>templates/launch-graphic.tsx</code></summary>

```tsx
// templates/launch-graphic.tsx
import { Canvas, Circle, Column, Heading, Image, Layer, Path, Rect, Row, Svg, Text, prop } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import { field, fitInside, formatDate, template } from "@hyper-elements/react/template";

// The brand's fonts and colors.
const FONTS = [
  { family: "Inter", src: "../fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf", weight: 400 },
  { family: "Inter", src: "../fonts/Inter-Bold.ttf", weight: 700 },
];
const [INK, PAPER, INDIGO, TEAL] = ["#15132e", "#f6f2ea", "#4f46e5", "#2dd4bf"];

// Each format's layout. It's the template's: no value changes it.
const LAYOUT = {
  square: { width: 1080, height: 1080, words: 952, headline: [72, 64, 56], text: 30, art: { width: 952, height: 420 }, shot: { width: 512, height: 320 } },
  landscape: { width: 1200, height: 630, words: 504, headline: [52, 46, 40], text: 23, art: { width: 552, height: 566 }, shot: { width: 456, height: 285 } },
} as const;

export default template({
  id: "acme.LaunchGraphic",
  version: "1.0.0",
  label: "Product launch graphic",
  guidance: "For product launches only. Sentence case, no emoji, no exclamation marks.",
  root: "Canvas",
  formats: { square: { width: 1080, height: 1080 }, landscape: { width: 1200, height: 630 } },
  fields: {
    headline: prop.text({ label: "Headline", required: true, maxLength: 90 }),
    features: prop.list(prop.text({ label: "Feature", maxLength: 40 }), { label: "Features", required: true, min: 3, max: 3 }),
    launchDate: prop.date({ label: "Launch date", required: true }),
    locale: prop.choice(["en-US", "de-DE"], { label: "Language", default: "en-US" }),
    screenshot: field.image({ label: "Product screenshot", required: true, fit: "contain", aspect: { min: 1.2, max: 2 }, minWidth: 1000, accepts: ["png"] }),
    artwork: field.image({ label: "Artwork", required: true, fit: "cover", maxCrop: 0.6, accepts: ["png"], guidance: "Bold flat shapes in the brand's colors. No text, logos or people." }),
  },
  // What only measuring decides has to hold: nothing past the Canvas, a font for every character, a headline that fits.
  rules: { require: { core: ["image/overflow", "image/glyph", "image/fit"] } },
  example: {
    headline: "Meet Orbit 3.0: release notes that write themselves",
    features: ["Drafts from merged PRs", "Your voice, every release", "Ships to Slack and email"],
    launchDate: "2026-12-03",
    screenshot: { src: "../designs/art/screenshot.png", width: 1600, height: 1000 },
    artwork: { src: "../designs/art/shapes.png", width: 1600, height: 1200 },
  },
  render(v, { format }) {
    const f = LAYOUT[format];
    const logo = <Image src={{ src: "./assets/orbit-logo.png", width: 252, height: 128 }} alt="Orbit" style={{ width: 126 }} />;
    const words = (
      <Column style={{ width: f.words, gap: 18 }}>
        {/* The date, written for the language, without its year. */}
        <Row style={{ gap: 10, alignItems: "center" }}>
          <Svg width={14} height={14}>
            <Circle cx={7} cy={7} r={7} style={{ fill: TEAL }} />
          </Svg>
          <Text field="launchDate" style={{ color: INDIGO, fontSize: f.text - 3, fontWeight: 700, lineHeight: 1.2, letterSpacing: 2, textTransform: "uppercase" }}>
            {formatDate(v.launchDate, v.locale, { month: "long", day: "numeric" })}
          </Text>
        </Row>
        {/* The headline is drawn at the largest size that fits it in three lines. What's under it follows it. */}
        <Heading field="headline" level={1} fit={{ sizes: [...f.headline], maxLines: 3 }} style={{ color: INK, lineHeight: 1.06, letterSpacing: -1.5 }}>
          {v.headline}
        </Heading>
        <Column style={{ gap: 8 }}>
          {v.features.map((feature, i) => (
            <Row key={i} style={{ gap: 12, alignItems: "center" }}>
              <Svg width={f.text - 2} height={f.text - 2} viewBox="0 0 24 24">
                <Circle cx={12} cy={12} r={12} style={{ fill: INDIGO }} />
                <Path d="M6.5 12.5 L10.5 16.5 L17.5 8.5" style={{ fill: "transparent", stroke: PAPER, strokeWidth: 2.6 }} />
              </Svg>
              <Text field={`features[${i}]`} style={{ color: "#3d3a57", fontSize: f.text, lineHeight: 1.3 }}>
                {feature}
              </Text>
            </Row>
          ))}
        </Column>
      </Column>
    );
    // The screenshot, shown whole in a window of the template's own, with the window's shadow behind it.
    const shot = fitInside(v.screenshot, f.shot);
    const [width, height] = [shot.width + 4, shot.height + 38];
    const product = (
      <Layer style={{ width: width + 12, height: height + 12, justifyItems: "start" }}>
        <Svg width={width + 12} height={height + 12}>
          <Rect x={12} y={12} width={width} height={height} rx={18} style={{ fill: INK }} />
        </Svg>
        <Column style={{ width, backgroundColor: PAPER, border: `2px solid ${INK}`, borderRadius: 18, overflow: "hidden" }}>
          <Row style={{ padding: [11, 14] }}>
            <Svg width={52} height={12}>
              <Circle cx={6} cy={6} r={6} style={{ fill: "#ff6b57" }} />
              <Circle cx={26} cy={6} r={6} style={{ fill: "#ffc93c" }} />
              <Circle cx={46} cy={6} r={6} style={{ fill: TEAL }} />
            </Svg>
          </Row>
          <Image field="screenshot" src={v.screenshot} alt="The product" style={shot} />
        </Column>
      </Layer>
    );
    // The artwork fills a panel, and the product sits in the middle of it.
    const art = (
      <Layer style={{ ...f.art, borderRadius: 32, alignItems: "center", justifyItems: "center" }}>
        <Image field="artwork" src={v.artwork} alt="" />
        {product}
      </Layer>
    );
    return (
      <Canvas width={f.width} height={f.height} fonts={FONTS} lang={v.locale} style={{ backgroundColor: PAPER, fontFamily: "Inter" }}>
        {format === "square" ? (
          // The logo at the top and the art at the bottom: the space around the words takes up the slack.
          <Column style={{ height: f.height, padding: 64, justifyContent: "space-between" }}>
            {logo}
            {words}
            {art}
          </Column>
        ) : (
          <Row style={{ height: f.height, padding: [32, 32, 32, 64], gap: 48 }}>
            <Column style={{ width: f.words, height: f.art.height, padding: [24, 0], justifyContent: "space-between" }}>
              {logo}
              {words}
            </Column>
            {art}
          </Row>
        )}
      </Canvas>
    );
  },
});
```

</details>

### Make a design

A design gives the template its values. From the shell, `design new` makes one from a brief (`brief.json`, the
values that are text) and the launch's pictures. `--set name=@file` gives an image by its file:

```bash
npx hyper-elements design new templates/launch-graphic.tsx -o designs/orbit.values.json \
  --values brief.json --set screenshot=@designs/art/screenshot.png --set artwork=@designs/art/shapes.png
```

`brief.json`:

```json
{
  "headline": "Meet Orbit 3.0: release notes that write themselves",
  "features": ["Drafts from merged PRs", "Your voice, every release", "Ships to Slack and email"],
  "launchDate": "2026-12-03"
}
```

It writes `designs/orbit.values.json`, a **values file**. That file is the design:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "template": {
    "module": "../templates/launch-graphic.tsx",
    "id": "acme.LaunchGraphic",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "sha256": "dbaf51a5c359…"
  },
  "formats": [
    "square",
    "landscape"
  ],
  "values": {
    "headline": "Meet Orbit 3.0: release notes that write themselves",
    "features": [
      "Drafts from merged PRs",
      "Your voice, every release",
      "Ships to Slack and email"
    ],
    "launchDate": "2026-12-03",
    "locale": "en-US",
    "screenshot": {
      "src": "./art/screenshot.png",
      "width": 1600,
      "height": 1000
    },
    "artwork": {
      "src": "./art/shapes.png",
      "width": 1600,
      "height": 1200
    }
  },
  "assets": {
    "screenshot": {
      "sha256": "e6d0855049bd…"
    },
    "artwork": {
      "sha256": "196b33139609…"
    }
  }
}
```

- **`version`** is the file format's own: `1`.
- **`template`** is the module it's made from (relative to this file), with its id and version, and a hash of the
  module as it was, so a template changed under the same version is noticed.
- **`formats`** are the ones it renders in. Take one out to render fewer.
- **`values`** are the brief's, the template's defaults (`locale`), and each picture with its size, read from its file.
- **`assets`** records each picture's hash, and where it came from once that's given.

The template checked the values before the file was written. Any program can write a values file of this shape: it's
checked again, by its template, every time it's read. [Values as data](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields#values-as-data)
says which keys one needs.

As TSX (`designs/orbit.tsx`, say), the same design is the template as its root, with the values as its props.
TypeScript checks them as they're written: a missing required field, a field the template doesn't have and a number given for text are type errors.

```tsx
import Launch from "../templates/launch-graphic";

export default () => (
  <Launch
    headline="Meet Orbit 3.0: release notes that write themselves"
    features={["Drafts from merged PRs", "Your voice, every release", "Ships to Slack and email"]}
    launchDate="2026-12-03"
    screenshot={{ src: "./art/screenshot.png", width: 1600, height: 1000 }}
    artwork={{ src: "./art/shapes.png", width: 1600, height: 1200 }}
  />
);
```

The command line checks and renders a TSX design as it does a values file, in every format. A `format="square"` prop
picks one. [The same from code](#the-same-from-code) renders one without the command line.

### Check it, then render it

```bash
npx hyper-elements check designs/orbit.values.json
```

```text
✓ designs/orbit.values.json [square] (Canvas)
  artwork (square): 952×420, needs 952×420px
  screenshot (square): 512×320, needs 512×320px
  fit headline: 72px (fits at 72, 64, 56)
  review artwork: Bold flat shapes in the brand's colors. No text, logos or people.
  review acme.LaunchGraphic: For product launches only. Sentence case, no emoji, no exclamation marks.
  review screenshot: Of unknown origin: no source is recorded for this image (give one with design set … --source)
  review artwork: Of unknown origin: no source is recorded for this image (give one with design set … --source)
✓ designs/orbit.values.json [landscape] (Canvas)
  artwork (landscape): 552×566, needs 552×566px
  screenshot (landscape): 456×285, needs 456×285px
  fit headline: 52px (fits at 52, 46, 40)
  review artwork: Bold flat shapes in the brand's colors. No text, logos or people.
  review acme.LaunchGraphic: For product launches only. Sentence case, no emoji, no exclamation marks.
  review screenshot: Of unknown origin: no source is recorded for this image (give one with design set … --source)
  review artwork: Of unknown origin: no source is recorded for this image (give one with design set … --source)
2 designs: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 skipped
```

Each format is checked on its own, and counts as a design in the last line: the values, the design the template
builds, and what can only be known by measuring it with its fonts.

- **`fit headline`** is the size the headline is drawn at.
- **Each picture's line** is its region and the pixels it needs.
- **`review`** lists what a person judges, which never fails a run: the template's `guidance`, and each picture with no
  record of where it came from, so a reviewer can tell a generated picture from a supplied one.
  `design set … --source artwork=source.json` records one ([sources](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/cli#values-files)).

```bash
npx hyper-elements render designs/orbit.values.json
```

```text
✓ designs/orbit.values.json [square] (Canvas) → out/designs/orbit.square.png
✓ designs/orbit.values.json [landscape] (Canvas) → out/designs/orbit.landscape.png
2 designs: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 skipped
```

Those are the two images above.

### Change one value

`design set` changes one value and keeps the rest. The template fits the new headline:

```bash
npx hyper-elements design set designs/orbit.values.json "headline=Meet Orbit 3.0: release notes that write themselves, in your voice"
```

<div class="output-gallery even">
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/orbit-landscape.png" title="Open the landscape launch graphic at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/orbit-landscape.png" width="1200" height="630" loading="lazy" alt="The landscape launch graphic with its first headline, drawn at 52px"></a><figcaption>51 characters: drawn at 52px</figcaption></figure>
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/long-landscape.png" title="Open the landscape launch graphic with the longer headline at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/long-landscape.png" width="1200" height="630" loading="lazy" alt="The landscape launch graphic with the longer headline, drawn at 40px in three lines, the date right above it and the features right under it"></a><figcaption>66 characters: drawn at 40px</figcaption></figure>
</div>

The landscape format's headline is narrow, so it's drawn at 40px, not 52px, in the same three lines. The date stays
right above it and the features right under it: the block is only as tall as its words. The square format still takes
it at 72px.

### Values it refuses

**A picture of the wrong shape.** The screenshot is 1.2:1 to 2:1. A banner in its place is refused when it's set, and the
file stays as it was:

<div class="output-gallery even">
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/art-screenshot.png" title="Open the product screenshot at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/art-screenshot.png" width="1600" height="1000" loading="lazy" alt="A product screenshot, 1600 by 1000 pixels"></a><figcaption>Taken: 1600×1000, 1.6:1</figcaption></figure>
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/art-banner.png" title="Open the banner at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/art-banner.png" width="1600" height="400" loading="lazy" alt="A wide banner, 1600 by 400 pixels"></a><figcaption>Refused: 1600×400, 4:1</figcaption></figure>
</div>

```bash
npx hyper-elements design set designs/orbit.values.json screenshot=@designs/art/banner.png
```

```text
✗ designs/orbit.values.json: not written
    error template/asset-aspect at values.screenshot: Product screenshot is 1600×400, 4:1; it takes 2:1 or narrower
```

**Copy that can't fit.** A headline inside its 90 characters can still be too long for the landscape format's three
lines at its smallest size. That's found when the design is measured: `check` exits 1, and `render` writes nothing for
a format that fails. The error's count of characters to cut is a rough estimate.

```bash
npx hyper-elements design set designs/orbit.values.json "headline=Meet Orbit 3.0: release notes that write themselves, in your own voice"
npx hyper-elements check designs/orbit.values.json
```

```text
✓ designs/orbit.values.json [square] (Canvas)
  artwork (square): 952×420, needs 952×420px
  screenshot (square): 512×320, needs 512×320px
  fit headline: 64px (fits at 64, 56)
  review artwork: Bold flat shapes in the brand's colors. No text, logos or people.
  review acme.LaunchGraphic: For product launches only. Sentence case, no emoji, no exclamation marks.
  review screenshot: Of unknown origin: no source is recorded for this image (give one with design set … --source)
  review artwork: Of unknown origin: no source is recorded for this image (give one with design set … --source)
✗ designs/orbit.values.json [landscape] (Canvas)
    error image/fit at root.children[0].children[0].children[1].children[1]: This Heading doesn't fit: it takes 4 lines at 40px, its smallest size, and fits 3: cut about 18 characters (required by acme.LaunchGraphic) Fix: Shorten the text, or give the template a smaller size
  rule image/fit (landscape): failed
  artwork (landscape): 552×566, needs 552×566px
  screenshot (landscape): 456×285, needs 456×285px
  fit headline: no size fits
  review artwork: Bold flat shapes in the brand's colors. No text, logos or people.
  review acme.LaunchGraphic: For product launches only. Sentence case, no emoji, no exclamation marks.
  review screenshot: Of unknown origin: no source is recorded for this image (give one with design set … --source)
  review artwork: Of unknown origin: no source is recorded for this image (give one with design set … --source)
2 designs: 1 error, 0 warnings, 0 skipped
```

## An email with a locked header and footer

<figure class="diagram"><a href="/generated/templates-guide/email-parts.svg" title="Open the diagram at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/email-parts.svg" width="832" height="380" alt="An email made from the Orbit email template, with its parts outlined. The header is locked. The body, which here holds a heading, three figures, a list and a button, is open. The footer, with the address and the unsubscribe link, is locked."></a></figure>

- **Locked:** the header and the footer. They're written in the template, so no email can change or drop them.
- **Open:** the body. It's a **slot** that takes any element, styled freely. Whoever writes the email, a person or an
  agent, writes only this.
- **Still checked:** the finished email, whatever the body holds. Its links go to Orbit's own domains, it has an
  unsubscribe link, and nothing is wider than the email.

The slot is one field, `render` places it between the two locked sections, and the rules hold whatever is written
there:

```tsx
// from templates/brand-email.tsx
fields: {
  preview: prop.text({ label: "Preview text", required: true, maxLength: 120 }),
  // Open: any element, styled freely. Whoever writes the email, a person or an agent, writes this.
  body: field.slot({ label: "Body", required: true, allow: "all", styles: "free" }),
},
```

```tsx
// from templates/brand-email.tsx
{/* Locked: the header. */}
<Section id="header" style={{ backgroundColor: "#0b1020", padding: [20, 32] }}>
  <Text style={{ color: "#ffffff", fontSize: 20, fontWeight: 700 }}>Orbit</Text>
</Section>
{/* Open: the body. */}
<Section id="body" field="body" style={{ backgroundColor: "#ffffff", padding: 32 }}>
  {v.body}
</Section>
{/* Locked: the footer, with the unsubscribe link every email needs. */}
<Section id="footer" style={{ padding: [20, 32] }}>
```

```tsx
// from templates/brand-email.tsx
rules: {
  plugins: { lint: lint({ kind: "marketing" }) },
  require: { lint: ["unsubscribe"], core: ["layout/overflow"] },
  links: { domains: ["orbit.example", "*.orbit.example"] },
},
```

<details>
<summary>The whole template: <code>templates/brand-email.tsx</code></summary>

```tsx
// templates/brand-email.tsx
import { Email, Link, Section, Text, prop } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import { field, template } from "@hyper-elements/react/template";
import { lint } from "@hyper-elements/lint";

export default template({
  id: "acme.BrandEmail",
  version: "1.0.0",
  label: "Orbit email",
  guidance: "Any email Orbit sends. The header and footer are Orbit's; the body is yours.",
  root: "Email",
  fields: {
    preview: prop.text({ label: "Preview text", required: true, maxLength: 120 }),
    // Open: any element, styled freely. Whoever writes the email, a person or an agent, writes this.
    body: field.slot({ label: "Body", required: true, allow: "all", styles: "free" }),
  },
  // Checked on the finished email, whatever the body holds.
  rules: {
    plugins: { lint: lint({ kind: "marketing" }) },
    require: { lint: ["unsubscribe"], core: ["layout/overflow"] },
    links: { domains: ["orbit.example", "*.orbit.example"] },
  },
  example: {
    preview: "A short note from the team at Orbit, with what changed this week",
    body: <Text>Hello from Orbit.</Text>,
  },
  render(v) {
    return (
      <Email lang="en" previewText={v.preview} style={{ backgroundColor: "#eef0f6" }}>
        {/* Locked: the header. */}
        <Section id="header" style={{ backgroundColor: "#0b1020", padding: [20, 32] }}>
          <Text style={{ color: "#ffffff", fontSize: 20, fontWeight: 700 }}>Orbit</Text>
        </Section>
        {/* Open: the body. */}
        <Section id="body" field="body" style={{ backgroundColor: "#ffffff", padding: 32 }}>
          {v.body}
        </Section>
        {/* Locked: the footer, with the unsubscribe link every email needs. */}
        <Section id="footer" style={{ padding: [20, 32] }}>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, color: "#5b6478" }}>
            Orbit, 1 Main Street. <Link href="https://orbit.example/unsubscribe">Unsubscribe from these emails</Link>
          </Text>
        </Section>
      </Email>
    );
  },
});
```

</details>

### Two emails, one template

An email is the template with a body. These two share nothing but the template:

<div class="output-gallery even">
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/welcome.png" title="Open the welcome email at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/welcome.png" width="680" height="351" loading="lazy" alt="A welcome email: Orbit's dark header, a heading, a paragraph and a button, and the footer with its unsubscribe link"></a><figcaption>designs/welcome.tsx: a heading, a paragraph, a button</figcaption></figure>
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/launch-week.png" title="Open the launch week email at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/launch-week.png" width="680" height="562" loading="lazy" alt="A launch week email: the same header and footer around three figures side by side, a divider, a list and a button"></a><figcaption>designs/launch-week.tsx: columns, a divider, a list</figcaption></figure>
</div>

```tsx
// designs/welcome.tsx
import { Button, Column, Heading, Text } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import BrandEmail from "../templates/brand-email";

export default () => (
  <BrandEmail
    preview="Your workspace is ready: here's how to publish your first release notes"
    body={
      <Column style={{ gap: 16 }}>
        <Heading level={1} style={{ fontSize: 28, color: "#0b1020" }}>Welcome to Orbit</Heading>
        <Text style={{ color: "#3b4254" }}>Your workspace is ready. Connect a repository, and Orbit drafts release notes from the pull requests you merge.</Text>
        <Button href="https://orbit.example/start" style={{ backgroundColor: "#4f46e5", color: "#ffffff", borderRadius: 8, padding: [12, 20], fontWeight: 700 }}>Connect a repository</Button>
      </Column>
    }
  />
);
```

<details>
<summary>The other email: <code>designs/launch-week.tsx</code></summary>

```tsx
// designs/launch-week.tsx
import { Button, Column, Divider, Heading, List, ListItem, Row, Text } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import BrandEmail from "../templates/brand-email";

const stat = (figure: string, label: string) => (
  <Column style={{ backgroundColor: "#f3f4ff", borderRadius: 12, padding: 16, gap: 4 }}>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 26, fontWeight: 700, color: "#4f46e5" }}>{figure}</Text>
    <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, color: "#3b4254" }}>{label}</Text>
  </Column>
);

export default () => (
  <BrandEmail
    preview="Launch week in numbers, what shipped, and what's next for Orbit"
    body={
      <Column style={{ gap: 20 }}>
        <Heading level={1} style={{ fontSize: 28, color: "#0b1020" }}>Launch week, in numbers</Heading>
        <Row style={{ gap: 12 }}>
          {stat("1,204", "teams joined")}
          {stat("38k", "notes drafted")}
          {stat("4.8", "average rating")}
        </Row>
        <Divider style={{ borderTop: "1px solid #e2e5ee" }} />
        <Heading level={2} style={{ fontSize: 18, color: "#0b1020" }}>What shipped</Heading>
        <List style={{ color: "#3b4254" }}>
          <ListItem>Release notes in your team's voice</ListItem>
          <ListItem>Exports in half the time</ListItem>
          <ListItem>Publishing to Slack and email</ListItem>
        </List>
        <Button href="https://orbit.example/changelog" style={{ backgroundColor: "#0b1020", color: "#ffffff", borderRadius: 8, padding: [12, 20], fontWeight: 700 }}>Read the changelog</Button>
      </Column>
    }
  />
);
```

</details>

```bash
npx hyper-elements render designs/welcome.tsx designs/launch-week.tsx
```

Each is checked by the template, then written as HTML and plain text (`out/designs/welcome.html` and
`welcome.txt`). The pictures are that HTML in Chromium.

### What the open body can't do

The body is open; the template's rules over the result aren't. An email that links outside Orbit's domains is refused,
with the link that broke the rule:

```tsx
// designs/off-site.tsx
import { Button, Column, Text } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import BrandEmail from "../templates/brand-email";

export default () => (
  <BrandEmail
    preview="A partner offer for Orbit customers, for a short time, from a friend of ours"
    body={
      <Column style={{ gap: 16 }}>
        <Text>Our friends at Northwind have an offer for Orbit customers.</Text>
        <Button href="https://northwind.example.net/offer">See the offer</Button>
      </Column>
    }
  />
);
```

```bash
npx hyper-elements check designs/off-site.tsx
```

```text
✗ designs/off-site.tsx (Email)
    error template/link-domain at root.children[1].children[0].children[1].props.href: northwind.example.net isn't one of acme.BrandEmail's domains (orbit.example, *.orbit.example) (required by acme.BrandEmail)
  rule links: failed
  review acme.BrandEmail: Any email Orbit sends. The header and footer are Orbit's; the body is yours.
1 design: 1 error, 0 warnings, 0 skipped
```

So whoever writes an email writes only its body: the header, the footer and the rules are the template's. In CI,
`--require-template acme.BrandEmail` fails any email that wasn't made from it.

A body written as JSX is code, though, and the command line runs it. Review these designs as you review any code.
For an agent whose work nobody reviews, use a template whose open parts are data, such as the
[invoice](#an-invoice-filled-from-data) below or a [digest of blocks](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots#blocks): a values file
runs nothing. See [what trusted templates guarantee](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/cli#what-that-guarantees-and-what-it-doesnt).

To open less, list the elements a slot takes and keep its styles to the brand's, as the next example does.

## A newsletter with a limited body

The email above opens its body completely. This newsletter's slot is narrow: the header and footer are locked, and
the body takes five kinds of element, in the brand's look, with one or two buttons. Its `subject` field is the title
drawn at the top of the email; the subject an inbox shows is set where the email is sent.

<div class="output-gallery single">
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/newsletter.png" title="Open the newsletter at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/newsletter.png" width="680" height="476" loading="lazy" alt="The June newsletter: Orbit's dark header, the title, two short sections with headings, a button, and a footer with an unsubscribe link"></a><figcaption>designs/june.tsx, rendered and drawn in Chromium</figcaption></figure>
</div>

The issue is the template with its values. What's inside `body` is the writer's:

```tsx
// designs/june.tsx
import { Button, Column, Heading, Text } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import Newsletter from "../templates/newsletter";

export default () => (
  <Newsletter
    subject="What's new in Orbit this June"
    preview="Release notes in your voice, faster exports, and an invitation to our open house"
    body={
      <Column>
        <Heading level={2}>Release notes in your voice</Heading>
        <Text>Orbit now learns how your team writes from the notes you've already published, and drafts the next ones the same way.</Text>
        <Heading level={2}>Faster exports</Heading>
        <Text>Exports finish in half the time, with no settings to change.</Text>
        <Button href="https://orbit.example/changelog">Read the changelog</Button>
      </Column>
    }
  />
);
```

An issue that styles its own heading and adds a table is refused, with what to change:

```bash
npx hyper-elements check designs/off-brand.tsx
```

```text
✗ designs/off-brand.tsx (Email)
    error template/slot-style at root.children[2].children[0].children[0].style.color: acme.Newsletter's body takes no styles of its own (styles: "none"): use the theme's named styles (style={{ apply: [...] }}) and variants, not color
    error template/slot-element at root.children[2].children[0].children[1]: A Table isn't one of the elements acme.Newsletter's body takes (Column, Heading, Text, Button, Link)
  review body: One to three short sections, each a Heading and a Text.
  review acme.Newsletter: Orbit's monthly newsletter. Friendly and plain: sentence case, no exclamation marks, no emoji.
1 design: 1 error, 0 warnings, 0 skipped
```

[Content: slots and blocks](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots#slots) has the whole newsletter template and every option.

## An invoice filled from data

<figure class="diagram"><a href="/generated/templates-guide/invoice-parts.svg" title="Open the diagram at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/invoice-parts.svg" width="896" height="706" alt="An invoice's A4 page made from the Orbit invoice template, with its parts outlined. The letterhead, the total and the footer are locked. The customer, the number and the two dates, the lines and the note are open fields."></a></figure>

- **Locked:** the letterhead, the table's columns, the total and the footer on every page, with its page number. The
  template adds the lines up, so a total is never typed.
- **Open:** fields, all of them data. A billing system or an agent writes an invoice's values as JSON, and never
  writes layout.
- **Formats:** A4 and Letter. One invoice renders as both.

```tsx
// from templates/invoice.tsx
formats: { a4: { size: "A4" }, letter: { size: "Letter" } },
// Open: what changes from one invoice to the next. All of it is data.
fields: {
  number: prop.text({ label: "Invoice number", required: true, pattern: "^INV-\\d{4}$" }),
  issued: prop.date({ label: "Issued", required: true }),
  due: prop.date({ label: "Due", required: true }),
```

The locked sum is ordinary code in `render`:

```tsx
// from templates/invoice.tsx
// Locked: the sums. The template adds them up, so a total is never typed.
const total = v.lines.reduce((sum, line) => sum + line.quantity * line.price, 0);
```

<details>
<summary>The whole template: <code>templates/invoice.tsx</code></summary>

```tsx
// templates/invoice.tsx
import { Circle, Column, Document, Heading, PageFooter, PageNumber, Row, Svg, Table, TableCell, TableRow, Text, prop } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import { formatDate, template } from "@hyper-elements/react/template";

const FONTS = [
  { family: "Inter", src: "../fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf", weight: 400 },
  { family: "Inter", src: "../fonts/Inter-Bold.ttf", weight: 700 },
];
const money = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "USD" });
const quiet = { fontSize: 11, color: "#5b6478" } as const;
const cell = { padding: [10, 0], border: { bottom: "1px solid #e2e5ee" } } as const;
const right = { ...cell, textAlign: "right" } as const;

/** A label over one field's value. */
const fact = (name: string, field: string, value: string) => (
  <Column style={{ gap: 2 }}>
    <Text style={quiet}>{name}</Text>
    <Text field={field} style={{ fontWeight: 700 }}>{value}</Text>
  </Column>
);

export default template({
  id: "acme.Invoice",
  version: "1.0.0",
  label: "Orbit invoice",
```
