```tsx
  guidance: "One invoice per customer per month. Describe each line as the customer's plan names it.",
  root: "Document",
  formats: { a4: { size: "A4" }, letter: { size: "Letter" } },
  // Open: what changes from one invoice to the next. All of it is data.
  fields: {
    number: prop.text({ label: "Invoice number", required: true, pattern: "^INV-\\d{4}$" }),
    issued: prop.date({ label: "Issued", required: true }),
    due: prop.date({ label: "Due", required: true }),
    customer: prop.object(
      {
        name: prop.text({ label: "Name", required: true, maxLength: 60 }),
        address: prop.list(prop.text({ label: "Address line", maxLength: 60 }), { label: "Address", required: true, min: 1, max: 4 }),
      },
      { label: "Billed to", required: true },
    ),
    lines: prop.list(
      prop.object(
        {
          description: prop.text({ label: "Description", required: true, maxLength: 80 }),
          quantity: prop.number({ label: "Quantity", required: true, min: 1 }),
          price: prop.number({ label: "Unit price", required: true, min: 0 }),
        },
        { label: "Line" },
      ),
      { label: "Lines", required: true, min: 1, max: 40 },
    ),
    note: prop.text({ label: "Note", maxLength: 200 }),
  },
  example: {
    number: "INV-0412",
    issued: "2026-12-01",
    due: "2026-12-31",
    customer: { name: "Northwind Traders", address: ["48 Harbor Road", "Portland, OR 97209"] },
    lines: [
      { description: "Orbit Team plan, December", quantity: 12, price: 29 },
      { description: "Extra workspaces", quantity: 2, price: 15 },
    ],
  },
  render(v, { format }) {
    // Locked: the sums. The template adds them up, so a total is never typed.
    const total = v.lines.reduce((sum, line) => sum + line.quantity * line.price, 0);
    return (
      <Document size={format === "letter" ? "Letter" : "A4"} margin={[56, 64, 48, 64]} title={`Invoice ${v.number}, Orbit`} lang="en" fonts={FONTS} style={{ backgroundColor: "#ffffff", fontFamily: "Inter", fontSize: 13, color: "#0b1020" }}>
        <Document.Page style={{ gap: 32 }}>
          {/* Locked: the letterhead. */}
          <Row id="letterhead" style={{ alignItems: "center" }}>
            <Row style={{ alignItems: "center", gap: 10 }}>
              <Svg width={26} height={26} title="Orbit">
                <Circle cx={13} cy={13} r={9} style={{ fill: "transparent", stroke: "#4f46e5", strokeWidth: 8 }} />
              </Svg>
              <Text style={{ fontSize: 22, fontWeight: 700 }}>Orbit</Text>
            </Row>
            <Column>
              <Text style={{ ...quiet, textAlign: "right" }}>1 Main Street, Springfield · billing@orbit.example</Text>
            </Column>
          </Row>

          <Heading level={1} style={{ fontSize: 40, lineHeight: 1.1 }}>Invoice</Heading>

          <Row style={{ alignItems: "start", gap: 24 }}>
            <Column id="customer" field="customer" style={{ gap: 2 }}>
              <Text style={quiet}>Billed to</Text>
              <Text style={{ fontWeight: 700 }}>{v.customer.name}</Text>
              {v.customer.address.map((line, i) => (
                <Text key={i}>{line}</Text>
              ))}
            </Column>
            <Row id="details" style={{ gap: 24 }}>
              {fact("Number", "number", v.number)}
              {fact("Issued", "issued", formatDate(v.issued, "en-US", { month: "short", day: "numeric" }))}
              {fact("Due", "due", formatDate(v.due, "en-US", { month: "short", day: "numeric" }))}
            </Row>
          </Row>

          <Table id="lines" field="lines">
            <TableRow header>
              <TableCell style={{ ...cell, ...quiet }}>Description</TableCell>
              <TableCell style={{ ...right, ...quiet, width: 60 }}>Qty</TableCell>
              <TableCell style={{ ...right, ...quiet, width: 100 }}>Unit price</TableCell>
              <TableCell style={{ ...right, ...quiet, width: 110 }}>Amount</TableCell>
            </TableRow>
            {v.lines.map((line, i) => (
              <TableRow key={i}>
                <TableCell style={cell}>{line.description}</TableCell>
                <TableCell style={right}>{String(line.quantity)}</TableCell>
                <TableCell style={right}>{money.format(line.price)}</TableCell>
                <TableCell style={right}>{money.format(line.quantity * line.price)}</TableCell>
              </TableRow>
            ))}
          </Table>

          <Column style={{ alignItems: "end" }}>
            <Column id="total" style={{ width: 210, gap: 2 }}>
              <Text style={{ ...quiet, textAlign: "right" }}>Total due</Text>
              <Text style={{ fontSize: 28, fontWeight: 700, lineHeight: 1.2, textAlign: "right", color: "#4f46e5" }}>{money.format(total)}</Text>
            </Column>
          </Column>

          {v.note ? <Text id="note" field="note" style={quiet}>{v.note}</Text> : null}
        </Document.Page>

        {/* Locked: the footer, on every page. */}
        <PageFooter id="footer">
          <Text style={{ ...quiet, padding: [12, 0, 0], border: { top: "1px solid #e2e5ee" } }}>
            Pay by bank transfer within 30 days, quoting the invoice number. Orbit Software, Inc., EIN 00-0000000. Page <PageNumber /> of <PageNumber total />
          </Text>
        </PageFooter>
      </Document>
    );
  },
});
```

</details>

### Make one, and render it

The invoice's values, as a billing system would write them (`invoice.json`). `design new` checks them and writes the
invoice's values file:

```json
{
  "number": "INV-0412",
  "issued": "2026-12-01",
  "due": "2026-12-31",
  "customer": { "name": "Northwind Traders", "address": ["48 Harbor Road", "Portland, OR 97209"] },
  "lines": [
    { "description": "Orbit Team plan, December", "quantity": 12, "price": 29 },
    { "description": "Extra workspaces", "quantity": 2, "price": 15 },
    { "description": "Onboarding session", "quantity": 1, "price": 250 }
  ],
  "note": "Thank you for a year with Orbit."
}
```

```bash
npx hyper-elements design new templates/invoice.tsx -o designs/northwind.values.json --values invoice.json
```

```text
✓ designs/northwind.values.json
  set number
  set issued
  set due
  set customer
  set lines
  set note
```

```bash
npx hyper-elements render designs/northwind.values.json --html
```

```text
✓ designs/northwind.values.json [a4] (Document) → out/designs/northwind.a4.pdf, out/designs/northwind.a4.html
✓ designs/northwind.values.json [letter] (Document) → out/designs/northwind.letter.pdf, out/designs/northwind.letter.html
2 designs: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 skipped
```

One PDF per format, drawn with `@react-pdf/renderer`. `--html` also writes each as print HTML, which is the page
pictured above, as Chromium draws it.

### What the invoice refuses

A number that isn't an invoice number is refused when it's set, and the file stays as it was:

```bash
npx hyper-elements design set designs/northwind.values.json number=NW-12
```

```text
✗ designs/northwind.values.json: not written
    error template/value at values.number: Invoice number: doesn't match ^INV-\d{4}$
```

A list of lines that's empty, a missing customer and a date that isn't one are refused the same way.
[Values: fields, images and formats](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields) lists every kind of field and its rules.

## The same from code

Nothing above needs the command line. This script renders an email whose root is a template, then checks a launch's
values and draws the image:

```tsx
// scripts/render.tsx
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { formatDiagnostics, render } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import { renderImage } from "@hyper-elements/react/image";
import Welcome from "../designs/welcome";
import Launch from "../templates/launch-graphic";

const bytes = (path: string) => new Uint8Array(readFileSync(path));
mkdirSync("out", { recursive: true });

// An email. The design's root is the template, so render() hands it to the template, which checks it first.
// A design the template refuses rejects here, with its problems.
const { html } = await render(<Welcome />);
writeFileSync("out/welcome.html", html);

// An image. Check the values, then draw the snapshot the check returned: what was checked is what's drawn.
const values = {
  headline: "Meet Orbit 3.0: release notes that write themselves",
  features: ["Drafts from merged PRs", "Your voice, every release", "Ships to Slack and email"],
  launchDate: "2026-12-03",
  screenshot: { src: "screenshot.png", width: 1600, height: 1000 },
  artwork: { src: "shapes.png", width: 1600, height: 1200 },
};
const checked = Launch.check(values, { format: "square" });
if (!checked.valid) throw new Error(formatDiagnostics(checked.diagnostics));

// Nothing is fetched: give each font the design names, and each image by the src it's written with.
const { image } = await renderImage(checked.snapshots.square!, {
  fonts: [
    { family: "Inter", src: bytes("fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf"), weight: 400 },
    { family: "Inter", src: bytes("fonts/Inter-Bold.ttf"), weight: 700 },
  ],
  images: {
    "screenshot.png": bytes("designs/art/screenshot.png"),
    "shapes.png": bytes("designs/art/shapes.png"),
    "./assets/orbit-logo.png": bytes("templates/assets/orbit-logo.png"),
  },
});
writeFileSync("out/launch.png", image);
```

- **`render()`** takes a design whose root is a template as it takes any design. So do `validate()`, `renderPdf()`
  (from `@hyper-elements/react/pdf`) and `renderImage()`: each hands the root to the template, and goes on with what
  it built. A design the template refuses rejects there with an `ElementsError`, as any design with errors does.
- **`check()`** never throws. It returns the problems, and a **snapshot** of the checked design for each format: draw
  that, and what was checked is what's drawn.
- **Fonts and images are given as bytes.** An image's key is the `src` the design names it by: the value's own, and
  the template's logo as the template wrote it.
- **`renderImage()` measures as it draws**, so the template's measured rules are decided there: a headline that
  doesn't fit rejects. There's nothing else to call.

[Rules, checks and diagnostics](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/rules) has everything `check()` returns.

---

# Values: fields, images and formats

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields

A template's **values** are what a design gives it as data. There are three ideas on this page:

<div class="concept-grid">
<a class="concept" href="#fields"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/concept-field.svg" width="600" height="400" alt="The launch graphic with only its headline lit and outlined: a field"><strong>Field</strong><span>One typed value: text, a date, a number, a choice, a list. The headline here is one.</span></a>
<a class="concept" href="#image-limits"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/concept-image.svg" width="600" height="400" alt="A product screenshot at 1.6 to 1 marked taken, and a banner at 4 to 1 marked refused: an image field's rules"><strong>Image field</strong><span>A picture, with limits on its shape, size and type. A banner isn't a screenshot.</span></a>
<a class="concept" href="#formats-and-the-example"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/concept-format.svg" width="600" height="400" alt="The launch graphic as a square image and as a landscape image: two formats"><strong>Format</strong><span>One of the sizes a template renders at. The same values give every one.</span></a>
</div>

[Template examples](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/examples) shows them at work; this page lists each one.

```tsx
import { prop } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import { field, template } from "@hyper-elements/react/template";
```

## Fields

A field is one open part of a template, declared in its `fields`. Most hold one typed value, made with a `prop` helper
from `@hyper-elements/react` or with `field.image()` from `@hyper-elements/react/template`. Two hold content, and have
[a page of their own](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots): `prop.blocks()` and `field.slot()`.

| Field | Its value | Its own options |
|-------|-----------|-----------------|
| `prop.text()` | Text | `maxLength`; `pattern`, a regular expression's source, matched with the `u` flag |
| `prop.date()` | A date, `YYYY-MM-DD` | |
| `prop.number()` | A number | `min`, `max` |
| `prop.choice(options)` | One of the options | |
| `prop.link()` | A URL | |
| `prop.list(item, { min, max })` | A list of one kind of item | Not given, it's `[]`, and its `min` applies to that too |
| `prop.object(fields)` | An object of named fields | Optional and not given, it's `undefined` |
| `prop.blocks(types, { min, max })` | A list of blocks, each one of the types | See [blocks](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots#blocks) |
| `field.image(limits)` | An image, `{ src, width, height }` | See [image limits](#image-limits) |
| `field.slot(options)` | JSX someone writes | See [slots](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots#slots) |

The other `prop` helpers (a color, a boolean and the rest) are fields too: they're the ones a
[custom element](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/custom-elements#props) declares its props with.

Every field takes these:

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `label` | Its name, for people: in messages and in `describe()` |
| `required` | A field is required only with `required: true`. Required text that's empty, or only spaces, counts as not given (`template/required`) |
| `default` | Filled in where the value isn't given |
| `guidance` | Plain English for whoever fills it. Never enforced: listed by `describe()`, and returned by `check()` as `review` items for a person to judge |

Lists and objects compose. A `field.image()` inside a list of objects keeps its limits, at `stories[1].image`.

A field can't be named `format`, `key`, `ref` or `children` (`template/field-name`): they're props of the template's
component.

## Image limits

An image field's value is `{ src, width, height }`, the file's size in px. Each limit is checked against what can
decide it: the size given, the file, or where the template draws it.

| Limit | It asks | Checked against | Where it fails |
|-------|---------|-----------------|----------------|
| `aspect: { min, max }` | Its width over its height | The size given | `template/asset-aspect` |
| `minWidth`, `minHeight` | Its smallest size in px | The size given | `template/asset-pixels` |
| `accepts` | Its type: `png`, `jpeg`, `gif`, `svg`, `webp` | Its name's extension, then its file | `template/asset-type` |
| `transparent` | `"required"` or `"forbidden"` | Its file | `template/asset-alpha` |
| `fit: "contain"` | Shown whole, at its own aspect | Where it's drawn | `template/asset-distorted`, `template/asset-cropped` |
| `fit: "cover"` | Cropped from the center to fill its region | Where it's drawn | |
| `maxCrop` | The most a `cover` image loses from either side, as a share (`0.6` is 60%) | Where it's drawn | `template/asset-cropped` |

Some facts can only be read from the file: whether it's transparent, its true size, its type where its name gives
none. Those are never taken as passed. Each is a note, `template/asset-unread`, until the file is read: by
[`checkLayout()`](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/rules#measured-rules-and-checklayout) given the file, or by the
[command line](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/cli), which reads a file beside the design. A file's header is read for PNG,
JPEG, GIF and SVG; a WebP is known by its name alone.

`fit` doesn't draw anything. It says how the template must show the picture, and the check holds the template to
it:

```tsx
// contain: sized to fit a box, at the picture's own aspect
<Image field="screenshot" src={v.screenshot} alt="The product" style={fitInside(v.screenshot, { width: 512, height: 320 })} />

// cover: the first child of a Layer fills the Layer's box, cut at its sides or its top and bottom
<Layer style={{ width: 952, height: 420 }}>
  <Image field="artwork" src={v.artwork} alt="" />
  {/* what's drawn over it */}
</Layer>
```

[Layout](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/layout#layer) has more on a `Layer`.

## Bindings

`field="…"` on a built-in element says which field it shows:

```tsx
<Heading field="headline">{v.headline}</Heading>
<ListItem field={`features[${i}]`}>{feature}</ListItem>
<Image field="stories[1].image" src={story.image} alt="" />
```

- **It's optional for text.** With it, a diagnostic on that node names its `field` (in `check()`'s result, and in the
  command line's `--json`), so a tool or an agent knows which value to change. Without it, the diagnostic has only
  the node's path.
- **An image with limits needs it:** it's how the template's checks find the image where it's drawn.
- **A slot needs it** on the one element that holds its content (`template/slot-host`).
- A `field` that names no field with a value is `template/unknown-binding`. An image field with rules that no node
  shows is `template/unbound`, a warning.
- A binding inside a custom element's own render is left out (`field/dropped`).

## Formats and the example

- **`formats`** are a template's named sizes: a Canvas's `{ width, height, scale }`, a Document's `{ size,
  orientation }`. A template with no formats has one size.
- **`render` builds each one.** It gets the format's name, and writes its root at that size and arranges the design
  for it. The size is written in both places on purpose: the template checks that what `render` built is the size its
  format declares (`template/format`).
- **`example`** is required: a full set of values. `describe()` lays it out, `check` of the template module checks it
  in every format, and tests render it.
- **`id`** is a namespace, a dot and a capitalized name (`acme.LaunchGraphic`). **`version`** is semver: a values file
  records it.

## Fitted text

In a Canvas, a `Heading` or a `Text` can be fitted: drawn at the largest of some sizes that keeps it within a number
of lines.

```tsx
<Heading field="headline" fit={{ sizes: [72, 64, 56], maxLines: 3 }}>{v.headline}</Heading>
```

It's how a template takes copy of different lengths without a size for each. Text that fits at none of its sizes is
`image/fit`, an error, found when the image is measured with its fonts. Three things share the word:

| | What it is |
|---|---|
| `fit={{ sizes, maxLines }}` on a `Heading` or a `Text` | Fitted text. Only in a Canvas |
| `image/fit` | The diagnostic for fitted text that doesn't fit. `image/…` codes are about the Canvas's image, not an image field |
| `fit: "contain"` or `"cover"` on an image field | How a picture fills its region. See [image limits](#image-limits) |

[Images](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/outputs/image#fitting-text-measuring-and-strict) has the rest: sizes as a range, several fitted texts,
and what's measured.

## Values as data

The same design can be data instead of TSX, for batches and tools: a values file. It holds the template's reference
and version, the formats, the values, and each asset's hash and where it came from.
[Template examples](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/examples#make-a-design) shows one whole. Its shape:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "template": { "module": "../templates/launch-graphic.tsx", "id": "acme.LaunchGraphic", "version": "1.0.0" },
  "formats": ["square", "landscape"],
  "values": { "headline": "…", "features": ["…", "…", "…"], "launchDate": "…" },
  "assets": { "artwork": { "sha256": "…", "source": { "kind": "generated" } } }
}
```

Any program can write one: with `toValuesFile()`, with the command line's `design new`, or as JSON of this shape. It
needs `version`, `template` (its `module`, `id` and `version`) and `values`, and `formats` where the template has
them; the hashes and `assets` are optional. It's checked by its template every time it's read. The command line
knows one by its name, `*.values.json`.

```ts
import { readValuesFile, toValuesFile } from "@hyper-elements/react/template";

const file = toValuesFile(launch, values, {
  module: "../templates/launch-graphic.tsx",
  formats: ["square", "landscape"],
  assets: { artwork: { sha256, source: { kind: "generated", provider, model, prompt } } },
});
const reopened = readValuesFile(JSON.parse(text), launch); // { values, migrated, formats, assets, diagnostics }
```

Defaults are written out, so a later minor release that changes one doesn't change the design.

Reading a file checks its template's id and version:

| The file was made with | Reading it |
|------------------------|------------|
| The same version | Reads its values |
| An older minor or patch | Reads its values, with a note (`template/upgraded`) |
| An older major | Runs the template's `migrate[major](values)` for each major between; without one, `template/version` |
| A newer version than the template | `template/version` |
| Another template | `template/id` |

A template's `migrate` is one function for each major version it can read from:

```tsx
migrate: {
  // From 1.x: the single `feature` became the list `features`.
  1: (values) => ({ ...values, features: [values.feature] }),
},
```

`readValuesFile()` also returns `migrated`: the file's values after its migrations ran and before they were checked.
A tool that repairs a file whose values aren't valid yet edits those.

Three more work with values in code. The first two are the template's own methods (`launch` here is the template);
the third is imported from `@hyper-elements/react/template`:

- `launch.update(values, patch)` changes some fields of checked values. What the patch doesn't name keeps its
  reference, an object is merged (JSON Merge Patch: `null` removes a key), and a list is replaced whole. It throws an
  `ElementsError` for a field the template doesn't have or a bad value.
- `launch.design(values, { format })` returns the plain root element, for code that has values in hand. It doesn't
  check them. To render what was checked, use the design `launch.check()` returns
  ([its snapshots](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/rules#snapshots)).
- `templateRequest(element)` gives a tool what a design's root asked for: the template, its props and its format.

## What describe() tells a filler

`launch.describe()` returns what whoever fills a template needs before starting: its formats, every field (its kind, whether
it's required, its JSON Schema, its image rules and guidance), a JSON Schema of all its values, and each image's region
in each format (its box, and the pixels it needs at the format's scale). For a `cover` image it adds the smallest size
that fills every region without upscaling, and what each format crops:

```json
{
  "path": "artwork",
  "kind": "image",
  "fit": "cover",
  "maxCrop": 0.6,
  "regions": { "square": { "box": [952, 420], "pixels": [952, 420] }, "landscape": { "box": [552, 566], "pixels": [552, 566] } },
  "suggested": { "width": 952, "height": 566, "crop": { "square": "cuts 26% of the height", "landscape": "cuts 42% of the width" } }
}
```

That's the launch graphic's artwork, as `npx hyper-elements describe templates/launch-graphic.tsx --json` prints it.

## Helpers

| Helper | What it gives |
|--------|---------------|
| `fitInside(image, box)` | The size that shows an image whole inside a box, at its own aspect |
| `sniffImage(bytes)` | An image file's `{ width, height, type, alpha }`, read from its header (PNG, JPEG, GIF, SVG), in plain JavaScript |
| `formatDate(date, locale, options)` | A date field written for a locale (`"3. Dezember"`, with `{ month: "long", day: "numeric" }`), in UTC, so the day is the one given and no clock is read |

---

# Content: slots and blocks

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots

Most [fields](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields) hold a value. A template can also leave room for **content**: whole
sections of a design. There are two ways, and they differ in who decides how the content looks. Both are declared in the
template's `fields`, beside its values:

<div class="concept-grid">
<a class="concept" href="#slots"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/concept-slot.svg" width="600" height="400" alt="An email with only its body lit and outlined: a slot"><strong>Slot</strong><span>A region someone writes freely, as JSX. The template limits which elements and styles it takes.</span></a>
<a class="concept" href="#blocks"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/concept-blocks.svg" width="600" height="400" alt="Two emails made of the same three section types, story, quote and button, in different orders: blocks"><strong>Blocks</strong><span>Sections picked from the types the template approves, and ordered, as data. Their look is the template's.</span></a>
</div>

| A template opens | For | Whoever fills it gives |
|------------------|-----|------------------------|
| A [field](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields) | One typed value | Text, a date, a list, an image |
| A [slot](#slots) | Content someone writes | JSX, with only the elements and styles the template allows |
| [Blocks](#blocks) | Sections picked and ordered | Data: each block's type and its fields |

## Slots

A slot is JSX the filler writes, inside limits the template sets. This newsletter's header and footer are locked,
its title is a text field, and its body is a slot.

<div class="output-gallery single">
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/newsletter.png" title="Open the newsletter at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/newsletter.png" width="680" height="476" loading="lazy" alt="The June newsletter: Orbit's dark header, the title, two short sections with headings, a button, and a footer with an unsubscribe link"></a><figcaption>designs/june.tsx, rendered and drawn in Chromium</figcaption></figure>
</div>

The template places the slot in a built-in element bound to it, its host (`<Section field="body">`), and everything
under the host is the slot's:

```tsx
// templates/newsletter.tsx
import { Button, Column, Email, Heading, Link, Section, Text, defineTheme, prop } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import { field, template } from "@hyper-elements/react/template";
import { lint } from "@hyper-elements/lint";

// The brand's look for what an issue is written with: the content sets no styles of its own.
const brand = defineTheme({
  elements: {
    Heading: { color: "#0b1020", by: { level: { 1: { fontSize: 30, lineHeight: 1.2 }, 2: { fontSize: 20, lineHeight: 1.3 } } } },
    Text: { color: "#3b4254", fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 1.6 },
    Button: { backgroundColor: "#4f46e5", color: "#ffffff", borderRadius: 8, padding: [12, 20], fontWeight: 700 },
    Column: { gap: 12 },
  },
});

export default template({
  id: "acme.Newsletter",
  version: "1.0.0",
  label: "Orbit newsletter",
  guidance: "Orbit's monthly newsletter. Friendly and plain: sentence case, no exclamation marks, no emoji.",
  root: "Email",
  fields: {
    subject: prop.text({ label: "Subject", required: true, maxLength: 70 }),
    preview: prop.text({ label: "Preview text", required: true, maxLength: 120 }),
    // What the issue's writer writes: these elements only, in the brand's look, with one or two buttons.
    body: field.slot({
      label: "Body",
      required: true,
      allow: [Column, Heading, Text, Button, Link],
      styles: "none",
      count: { Button: { min: 1, max: 2 } },
      guidance: "One to three short sections, each a Heading and a Text.",
    }),
  },
  rules: {
    plugins: { lint: lint({ kind: "marketing" }) },
    // An unsubscribe link, link text that says where it goes, a language, and nothing wider than the email.
    require: { lint: ["unsubscribe", "link-text", "lang"], core: ["layout/overflow"] },
    // Links go to Orbit's own domains.
    links: { domains: ["orbit.example", "*.orbit.example"] },
    root: { lang: true, previewText: true },
  },
  example: {
    subject: "What's new in Orbit this month",
    preview: "Faster exports, release notes in your voice, and an invitation to our open house",
    body: (
      <Column>
        <Heading level={2}>Faster exports</Heading>
        <Text>Exports now finish in half the time, with no settings to change.</Text>
        <Button href="https://orbit.example/changelog">Read the changelog</Button>
      </Column>
    ),
  },
  render(v) {
    return (
      <Email lang="en" previewText={v.preview} theme={brand} style={{ backgroundColor: "#eef0f6" }}>
        <Section style={{ backgroundColor: "#0b1020", padding: [20, 32] }}>
          <Text style={{ color: "#ffffff", fontSize: 20, fontWeight: 700 }}>Orbit</Text>
        </Section>
        <Section style={{ backgroundColor: "#ffffff", padding: [32, 32, 8] }}>
          <Heading field="subject" level={1}>{v.subject}</Heading>
        </Section>
        <Section field="body" style={{ backgroundColor: "#ffffff", padding: [16, 32, 32] }}>
          {v.body}
        </Section>
        <Section style={{ padding: [20, 32] }}>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, color: "#5b6478" }}>
            Orbit, 1 Main Street. <Link href="https://orbit.example/unsubscribe">Unsubscribe from these emails</Link>
          </Text>
        </Section>
      </Email>
    );
  },
});
```

An issue is the template with its values. What's inside `body` is the writer's:

```tsx
// designs/june.tsx
import { Button, Column, Heading, Text } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import Newsletter from "../templates/newsletter";

export default () => (
  <Newsletter
    subject="What's new in Orbit this June"
    preview="Release notes in your voice, faster exports, and an invitation to our open house"
    body={
      <Column>
        <Heading level={2}>Release notes in your voice</Heading>
        <Text>Orbit now learns how your team writes from the notes you've already published, and drafts the next ones the same way.</Text>
        <Heading level={2}>Faster exports</Heading>
        <Text>Exports finish in half the time, with no settings to change.</Text>
        <Button href="https://orbit.example/changelog">Read the changelog</Button>
      </Column>
    }
  />
);
```

An issue that styles its own heading and adds a table is refused, with what to change:

```tsx
// designs/off-brand.tsx
import { Button, Column, Heading, Table, TableCell, TableRow, Text } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import Newsletter from "../templates/newsletter";

export default () => (
  <Newsletter
    subject="Huge summer sale"
    preview="Everything is on sale this week, for a short time only, across the whole store"
    body={
      <Column>
        <Heading level={2} style={{ color: "#ff0066" }}>Everything must go</Heading>
        <Table><TableRow><TableCell><Text>Pro plan</Text></TableCell><TableCell><Text>50% off</Text></TableCell></TableRow></Table>
        <Button href="https://orbit.example/sale">Shop the sale</Button>
      </Column>
    }
  />
);
```

```bash
npx hyper-elements check designs/off-brand.tsx
```

```text
✗ designs/off-brand.tsx (Email)
    error template/slot-style at root.children[2].children[0].children[0].style.color: acme.Newsletter's body takes no styles of its own (styles: "none"): use the theme's named styles (style={{ apply: [...] }}) and variants, not color
    error template/slot-element at root.children[2].children[0].children[1]: A Table isn't one of the elements acme.Newsletter's body takes (Column, Heading, Text, Button, Link)
  review body: One to three short sections, each a Heading and a Text.
  review acme.Newsletter: Orbit's monthly newsletter. Friendly and plain: sentence case, no exclamation marks, no emoji.
1 design: 1 error, 0 warnings, 0 skipped
```

### What a slot allows

Two options set a slot's limits: which elements its content may use (`allow`), and how it may style them (`styles`).

| Option | What it sets | Refused as |
|--------|--------------|------------|
| `allow: [Column, Heading, …]` | The elements the content may use, given as the elements themselves | `template/slot-element` |
| `allow: "all"` | Every built-in the template's root may hold, but the roots and `Html`. `deny: [Table, Video]` takes some out; `["all", ProductCard]` adds your own | `template/slot-element` |
| `count: { Button: { min: 1, max: 2 } }` | How many of a type, counting what's shown at some width | `template/slot-count` |

`styles` has three settings, from the brand's look only to anything:

| `styles` | The content may | An example |
|----------|-----------------|------------|
| `"none"` | Set no style of its own. It gets the theme's look for each element, and may use the theme's named styles and variants where the theme has them | `<Text>` and `<Button variant="secondary">`, never `style={{ color: … }}` |
| `"theme"` (the default) | Style freely, with every brand value taken from the theme | `style={{ color: token("colors.primary"), textAlign: "center" }}` |
| `"free"` | Use any style | `style={{ color: "#ff0000" }}` |

Under `"theme"`, the brand's values come from the template's [theme](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/themes): `token("colors.primary")` stands
for the theme's primary color. A value written out where a token belongs is refused, with the style named:

```tsx
import { token } from "@hyper-elements/react";

<Text style={{ color: token("colors.primary") }}>Paid</Text>   // taken: the theme's color
<Text style={{ textAlign: "center" }}>Paid</Text>              // taken: not a brand value
<Text style={{ color: "#ff0000" }}>Paid</Text>                 // template/slot-style: color is a literal
<Column style={{ padding: 12 }}>…</Column>                     // template/slot-style: each side a token() or 0
```

- **The newsletter above is `"none"`**, and its theme only gives each element its look. So its content sets no style
  at all, and has no named style or variant to use.
- **A brand value** is a color, a font, a spacing (`padding`, `gap`, `rowGap`), a radius, a border's color, and
  `fontSize`, `lineHeight` and `letterSpacing`, in `style` and in its `mobile` and `hover` blocks. Alignment, widths
  and the rest aren't.
- **A built-in is allowed by its type, a [custom element](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/custom-elements) by its definition.** Content that
  defines its own `acme.ProductCard` is refused ("not the template's"), and its render never runs. A root and `Html`
  are never allowed.
- **`allow: "all"` widens with Elements:** a later release that adds a built-in adds it to the slot. A template that
  wants a fixed set across upgrades writes a list.
- **Content never sets** `attrs` (`template/slot-attrs`), or, under `"none"` and `"theme"`, `tokens` or `theme`
  (`template/slot-tokens`). A `field` inside it is its own (`template/slot-field`): the template reads no binding there.
- **The content must be what its host may hold**, as any children are. A Section holds a Column, a Row or any
  content element (a Text, a Button), but not another Section. Several elements go in a `Column` or a fragment
  (`<>…</>`), not an array.
- **The subject line isn't the design's.** The newsletter's `subject` field is its title, drawn in the email; the
  subject an inbox shows is set where the email is sent.

### The template never sees the content

A template's render runs with a mark in the slot's place, so its locked parts can't depend on what's written there.
The content is rendered on its own (it sees none of the template's React context) and put in at the mark. The mark
goes in exactly one element bound to the slot (`template/slot-host`).

### A slot stored as data

A values file is JSON, so it can't hold JSX. It stores a slot one of two ways:

| Stored as | It is | To check it |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| `{ "module": "./_slots/june.body.tsx" }` | A module whose default export renders the content | The module has to be run first, and what it rendered given to `check()` in `fragments`. The [command line](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/cli#slots-stored-as-modules) does that, in a process of its own |
| `{ "fragment": … }` | The content already rendered and recorded as data, by `captureFragment()` | `check()` reads it itself |

A slot module is a component with nothing around it:

```tsx
// designs/_slots/june.body.tsx
import { Button, Column, Heading, Text } from "@hyper-elements/react";

export default () => (
  <Column>
    <Heading level={2}>Faster exports</Heading>
    <Text>Exports finish in half the time.</Text>
    <Button href="https://orbit.example/changelog">Read the changelog</Button>
  </Column>
);
```

From code, `captureFragment()` renders content and records it. Give it as the slot's value, or in `fragments` for a
slot stored as its module:

```tsx
import { captureFragment } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import Body from "./designs/_slots/june.body";

const body = captureFragment(<Body />);
newsletter.check({ subject, preview, body: { fragment: body } });                                              // the content itself
newsletter.check({ subject, preview, body: { module: "./_slots/june.body.tsx" } }, { fragments: { body } });   // the module's, run here
```

`toValuesFile()` stores a slot's JSX as its fragment. Without a module's content, `check()` gives
`template/slot-unloaded`. Store a module where people edit the content as a file; store a fragment where a tool wrote
it and nothing should run to read it back.

## Blocks

`prop.blocks(types, { min, max })` is a list of approved section types, each a `prop.object()`. The filler picks
which, in what order, and fills them; the look is the template's. These two digests are one template, with three types:

<div class="output-gallery even">
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/digest-monday.png" title="Open Monday's digest at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/digest-monday.png" width="680" height="430" loading="lazy" alt="A digest email: a story, then a customer's quote, then a button"></a><figcaption>A story, a quote, a button</figcaption></figure>
<figure><a href="/generated/templates-guide/digest-friday.png" title="Open Friday's digest at full size"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/digest-friday.png" width="680" height="446" loading="lazy" alt="A digest email: a customer's quote, then two stories"></a><figcaption>A quote, two stories</figcaption></figure>
</div>

Each digest's body is a list: every item names its type and gives that type's values. Monday's
(`digest-monday.json`):

```json
{
  "preview": "Faster exports, what a customer said about them, and the changelog",
  "body": [
    { "type": "story", "title": "Faster exports", "text": "Exports finish in half the time, with no settings to change." },
    { "type": "quote", "text": "Our release notes went out before the standup ended.", "by": "Dana, Northwind Traders" },
    { "type": "button", "label": "Read the changelog", "href": "https://orbit.example/changelog" }
  ]
}
```

The template lists the types, and draws each one:

```tsx
// from templates/digest.tsx
body: prop.blocks(
  {
    story: prop.object({ title: prop.text({ label: "Title", required: true, maxLength: 60 }), text: prop.text({ label: "Text", required: true, maxLength: 240 }) }, { label: "Story" }),
    quote: prop.object({ text: prop.text({ label: "Quote", required: true, maxLength: 140 }), by: prop.text({ label: "Who said it", required: true, maxLength: 60 }) }, { label: "Quote" }),
    button: prop.object({ label: prop.text({ label: "Label", required: true, maxLength: 30 }), href: prop.link({ label: "Link", required: true }) }, { label: "Button" }),
  },
  { label: "Body", required: true, min: 1, max: 6 },
),
```

```tsx
// from templates/digest.tsx
{v.body.map((block, i) =>
  block.type === "story" ? (
    <Section key={i} id={`story-${i}`} style={{ backgroundColor: "#ffffff", padding: [24, 32], gap: 8 }}>
      <Heading level={2} field={`body[${i}].title`} style={{ fontSize: 20, color: "#0b1020" }}>{block.title}</Heading>
      <Text field={`body[${i}].text`} style={{ color: "#3b4254" }}>{block.text}</Text>
    </Section>
  ) : block.type === "quote" ? (
```

A block of a type the template doesn't list is refused, with the types it has:

```bash
npx hyper-elements design set designs/digest-monday.values.json "body=[{\"type\":\"video\"}]"
```

```text
✗ designs/digest-monday.values.json: not written
    error template/value at values.body[0]: A block is { type, … } with type "story" or "quote" or "button", not "video"
```

<details>
<summary>The whole template: <code>templates/digest.tsx</code></summary>

```tsx
// templates/digest.tsx
import { Button, Email, Heading, Link, Section, Text, prop } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import { template } from "@hyper-elements/react/template";
import { lint } from "@hyper-elements/lint";

export default template({
  id: "acme.Digest",
  version: "1.0.0",
  label: "Orbit digest",
  guidance: "A short digest. Lead with the news; one button at most.",
  root: "Email",
  fields: {
    preview: prop.text({ label: "Preview text", required: true, maxLength: 120 }),
    // Open: which sections, and in what order. Each is one of three approved types, filled as data.
    body: prop.blocks(
      {
        story: prop.object({ title: prop.text({ label: "Title", required: true, maxLength: 60 }), text: prop.text({ label: "Text", required: true, maxLength: 240 }) }, { label: "Story" }),
        quote: prop.object({ text: prop.text({ label: "Quote", required: true, maxLength: 140 }), by: prop.text({ label: "Who said it", required: true, maxLength: 60 }) }, { label: "Quote" }),
        button: prop.object({ label: prop.text({ label: "Label", required: true, maxLength: 30 }), href: prop.link({ label: "Link", required: true }) }, { label: "Button" }),
      },
      { label: "Body", required: true, min: 1, max: 6 },
    ),
  },
  rules: {
    plugins: { lint: lint({ kind: "marketing" }) },
    require: { lint: ["unsubscribe", "lang"] },
    links: { domains: ["orbit.example", "*.orbit.example"] },
  },
  example: {
    preview: "This week at Orbit: one story, and where to read the rest of it",
    body: [
      { type: "story", title: "Faster exports", text: "Exports finish in half the time, with no settings to change." },
      { type: "button", label: "Read the changelog", href: "https://orbit.example/changelog" },
    ],
  },
  render(v) {
    return (
      <Email lang="en" previewText={v.preview} style={{ backgroundColor: "#eef0f6" }}>
        <Section style={{ backgroundColor: "#0b1020", padding: [20, 32] }}>
          <Text style={{ color: "#ffffff", fontSize: 20, fontWeight: 700 }}>Orbit</Text>
        </Section>
        {/* Each block's look is the template's: its type picks which. */}
        {v.body.map((block, i) =>
          block.type === "story" ? (
            <Section key={i} id={`story-${i}`} style={{ backgroundColor: "#ffffff", padding: [24, 32], gap: 8 }}>
              <Heading level={2} field={`body[${i}].title`} style={{ fontSize: 20, color: "#0b1020" }}>{block.title}</Heading>
              <Text field={`body[${i}].text`} style={{ color: "#3b4254" }}>{block.text}</Text>
            </Section>
          ) : block.type === "quote" ? (
            <Section key={i} id={`quote-${i}`} style={{ backgroundColor: "#f3f4ff", padding: [24, 32], gap: 8 }}>
              <Text field={`body[${i}].text`} style={{ fontSize: 20, lineHeight: 1.4, color: "#4f46e5" }}>“{block.text}”</Text>
              <Text field={`body[${i}].by`} style={{ fontSize: 14, color: "#5b6478" }}>{block.by}</Text>
            </Section>
          ) : (
            <Section key={i} id={`button-${i}`} style={{ backgroundColor: "#ffffff", padding: [24, 32] }}>
              <Button field={`body[${i}].label`} href={block.href} style={{ backgroundColor: "#0b1020", color: "#ffffff", padding: [12, 20], fontWeight: 700 }}>{block.label}</Button>
            </Section>
          ),
        )}
        <Section style={{ padding: [20, 32] }}>
          <Text style={{ fontSize: 14, color: "#5b6478" }}>
            Orbit, 1 Main Street. <Link href="https://orbit.example/unsubscribe">Unsubscribe from these emails</Link>
          </Text>
        </Section>
      </Email>
    );
  },
});
```

</details>

As TSX, the same list is the template's prop: `<Digest preview="…" body={[{ type: "story", title: "…", text: "…" }]} />`.

Blocks can hold any field, an image with its limits among them:

```tsx
fields: {
  body: prop.blocks(
    {
      hero: prop.object({ title: prop.text({ label: "Title", required: true }), image: field.image({ label: "Image", fit: "contain" }) }, { label: "Hero" }),
      quote: prop.object({ text: prop.text({ label: "Quote", required: true, maxLength: 120 }) }, { label: "Quote" }),
    },
    { label: "Body", required: true, min: 1, max: 6 }
  ),
},
// values: { body: [{ type: "hero", title: "Orbit is live" }, { type: "quote", text: "Ship small." }] }
```

- `type` names each block's type, so a block type can't have a field named `type` (`template/block-type`).
- An unknown or missing type is `template/value`, naming the types.
- Limits and bindings inside a block work as anywhere: `body[0].image`.

Whatever fills a slot or a list of blocks, the template's [rules](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/rules#rules-over-the-result)
are checked on the finished design.

## Annotated templates

A template with one size and fields of text, links, images and slots can be written as the design itself, with what's
open marked where it is. It's `open` and `design` in place of `fields` and `render` (the theme and the header and
footer components are left out here):

```tsx
import { field, open, template } from "@hyper-elements/react/template";

const title = open(prop.text({ label: "Title", required: true, maxLength: 70 }));
const body = open(field.slot({ label: "Body", required: true, allow: "all", styles: "theme" }));

export default template({
  id: "acme.Announcement",
  version: "1.0.0",
  rules: { plugins: { lint: lint({ kind: "marketing" }) }, require: { lint: ["unsubscribe"] } },
  open: { title, body },
  design: (
    <Email width={600} theme={brand}>
      <BrandHeader />
      <Heading field={title}>What's new at Acme</Heading>
      <Section field={body}>
        <Text>Three things shipped this week.</Text>
      </Section>
      <BrandFooter />
    </Email>
  ),
});
```

A marker goes on a built-in written in `design` itself, and what the marked node holds is the example:

| A marker for | Goes on |
|--------------|---------|
| A text field | A Heading, Text, ListItem, Button or Link holding its example text |
| A link | A Link's or Button's `href` |
| An image (`field.image()`) | An Image's `src` |
| A slot | The node that holds its content |

A template with formats, lists, blocks or computed values uses `fields` and `render`.

---

# Rules, checks and diagnostics

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/rules

A **rule** is something that must hold on the finished design, whatever filled it. A **check** is the template
testing one design: its values, then the design they build, then its rules. A **diagnostic** is what a check says when
something fails, with what to change.

<div class="concept-grid single">
<a class="concept" href="#rules-over-the-result"><img src="/generated/templates-guide/concept-rule.svg" width="600" height="400" alt="An email whose button links to another company's site, the button outlined in red and the email refused: a rule"><strong>Rule</strong><span>This template's links go to its own domains. An email with any other link is refused, and the check says which.</span></a>
</div>

[Template examples](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/examples) shows checks from the command line; this page is the reference.

## Rules over the result

Rules are checked on the finished design, whatever filled it: values, blocks or a slot's content.

```tsx
import { lint } from "@hyper-elements/lint";

rules: {
  plugins: { lint: lint({ kind: "marketing" }) },
  require: {
    lint: ["unsubscribe", "preview-text", "contrast", "link-text", "lang"],
    core: ["layout/overflow"],
  },
  links: { domains: ["acme.com", "*.acme.com"], params: { utm_source: "newsletter" }, schemes: ["mailto"] },
  images: { domains: ["cdn.acme.com"] },
  root: { lang: true },
},
```

| Rule | It requires | Where it fails |
|------|-------------|----------------|
| `require.lint` | [Lint's rules](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/lint), by id: a finding of one is an error, with "(required by …)" | The lint rule's own code |
| `require.core` | Checks of Elements' own, by their codes: the [list below](#what-requirecore-takes) | That code |
| `links.domains` | Every http(s) link's host: `acme.com` itself, `*.acme.com` its subdomains | `template/link-domain` |
| `links.params` | A query parameter on every link | `template/link-param` |
| `links.schemes` | The other schemes a link may use (`mailto`) | `template/link-scheme` |
| | A relative link is refused | `template/link-relative` |
| `images.domains` | Every image's host: an Image's, a Video's thumbnail, a Social's icons. Off unless given; with it, an image from any other host, inline (`data:`) or relative is refused | `template/image-domain` |
| `root` | Root props that must be set. For a prop `render` takes from a value that may be missing, such as an optional language | `template/root-prop` |

Each required rule ends `passed`, `failed` or `not-run`, in `check()`'s `rules`. One that didn't run never counts as
passed.

- **`plugins.lint`** is `lint()` from `@hyper-elements/lint`, as you'd configure it for any design. `require.lint`
  names the rules of it a design must pass.
- **Whether lint has each required rule is checked when the template is defined,** before any design. A rule lint
  doesn't have, one that's off as lint is configured (`unsubscribe` needs `kind: "marketing"`), or one that doesn't
  run on the template's root (lint checks Emails and Pages) is `template/rule-unavailable`. If lint itself throws, its
  rules are `not-run`, an error (`template/rule-not-run`).
- **A Canvas's `image/…` rules are decided when the image is measured.** `check()` leaves them `not-run`, and
  `renderImage()` decides them as it draws. See [measured rules](#measured-rules-and-checklayout).
- **Links are checked everywhere:** in locked parts and a Menu's too. A URL with a sending service's tag (`{{…}}`) still
  has its host checked where it's written out: `https://evil.example/?id={{contact.id}}` fails `links.domains`. Only a
  host that is itself a tag (`{{unsubscribe_url}}`, `https://{{host}}/`) can't be checked, so the link is listed for
  review, or refused with `tags: "deny"` (`template/link-tag`). A tagged URL's query parameters are the service's to
  fill, so `links.params` doesn't check them.
- **Images are checked everywhere too,** with `images.domains`: in locked parts, slots and blocks. An image whose host
  is a sending service's tag can't be checked, and is refused. A YouTube video with no thumbnail of its own shows
  YouTube's, from `img.youtube.com`: give it a thumbnail, or list that host. The Social element's icons load from its
  icon host, which the message names.
- **`plugins.other`** runs other plugins (email-clients'), whose findings are reported but can't be required.

### What require.core takes

| Code | What it finds | Runs on |
|------|---------------|---------|
| `layout/overflow` | Content wider than the space it has | Every root |
| `layout/shrunk` | A Row's children narrowed, because their widths add up to more than it has | Every root |
| `document/overflow` | A page's content that looks taller than the page (an estimate) | Document |
| `canvas/overflow` | A Canvas's content that looks taller than the Canvas (an estimate, made before it's measured) | Canvas |
| `image/overflow` | Content that runs past the Canvas, measured | Canvas |
| `image/glyph` | A character no font given has | Canvas |
| `image/fit` | [Fitted text](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/fields#fitted-text) that fits at none of its sizes | Canvas |

Requiring a check does two things. A finding of it is an error, with "(required by …)", where on a design of its own
most of these are warnings. And the check has to have run: `check()` reports it `not-run` until it has, and a design
with a required rule that hasn't run can't be rendered. That's what stops a Canvas passing on its values alone, before
anything measured it.

## check()

`check()` is a template's own method. `launch.check(values, { format })` never throws. It checks one format: a
template with several needs one named. It returns
`{ valid, values, diagnostics, review, rules, snapshots, template }`:

```ts
import { formatDiagnostics } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import launch from "./templates/launch-graphic";

const checked = launch.check(values, { format: "square" });
if (!checked.valid) console.error(formatDiagnostics(checked.diagnostics));
```

[The same from code](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/examples#the-same-from-code) is a whole script: it checks a launch's
values, then draws the image with its fonts and pictures.

| It returns | What it is |
|------------|------------|
| `valid` | Whether nothing is an error |
| `values` | The values as read: defaults filled in |
| `diagnostics` | What it found, each with its `code`, `path` and `message` |
| `review` | Each field's `guidance` and the template's own, for a person to judge. Never an error |
| `rules` | Each required rule: `passed`, `failed` or `not-run` |
| `snapshots` | The checked design, by the format's name (`default` for a template with one size), where it's valid |
| `template` | Its `id` and `version` |

It checks in two steps:

1. **The values**, by their fields: unknown fields, missing required ones, values a field refuses, lists outside their
   counts, and each image's declared size and name against its rules.
2. **The design it builds in each format**, as `validate()` checks any design, and what only the template knows: its
   root and its format's size, its bindings, how each bound image is shown, a slot's content against its limits, and
   the rules over the result.

The second step catches the template's own mistakes, not only bad values: a `contain` image drawn at another aspect
than its file's, say.

`check(element)`, a function imported from `@hyper-elements/react/template`, checks a design whose root is a template
(`<Launch … />`), in its `format` or, without one, in every format, as the command line does.

## Snapshots

A **snapshot** is the checked design, built once and recorded as plain data. `check()` returns one for each format.
`render()`, `validate()`, `prepare()`, `inspect()`, `renderPdf()` and `renderImage()` take one in place of an element,
and never build it again.

So what was checked is what's rendered: a slot's content that would render something else the second time never gets
a second time. Rendering `launch.design()`'s element instead runs a slot's code again, unchecked.

## Measured rules and checkLayout()

Some things can only be known by laying the design out with its real fonts and files: whether fitted text fits,
whether anything runs past the Canvas, whether a font has every character. That's **measuring**, and only a Canvas is
measured. A required rule that needs it is `not-run` after `check()`.

You rarely measure by hand:

| To | Use | What it does with the measured rules |
|----|-----|--------------------------------------|
| Draw the image | `renderImage()` | Measures as it draws, strictly: a missing font or content past the Canvas is an error, not a warning. A required rule that fails rejects, naming the rule |
| Check or render from the shell | The command line | Measures each format, and reports each rule |
| Get the report without drawing | `layoutImage()`, then `checkLayout()` | Returns each image's region, each fitted size and each rule's result. It doesn't draw, and doesn't change the snapshot |

Anything else that writes output from a Canvas's snapshot with a required rule still `not-run` refuses it
(`template/rule-not-run`): `render()`, which writes a Canvas's HTML preview, can't measure, and a rule that didn't
run never counts as passed.

```ts
import { layoutImage } from "@hyper-elements/react/image";
import { checkLayout, sniffImage } from "@hyper-elements/react/template";

// fonts and images: as renderImage() takes them, each as bytes.
const checked = launch.check(values, { format: "square" });
const layout = await layoutImage(checked.snapshots.square!, { fonts, images, scale: 2 });
const report = checkLayout(launch, checked.values, { format: "square", layout, files: { artwork: sniffImage(artworkBytes)! }, checked });
// report: { regions, fits, rules, diagnostics }
```

It takes the checked values (to find each image field), the measured `layout`, each image's `files` where you have
them, and `checked` itself so `rules` comes back whole: what `check()` decided, with the measured ones added.

`checkLayout()` is synchronous and pure. It gives:

| It gives | What it is |
|----------|------------|
| `regions` | Each bound image's box, and the pixels it needs at the scale it's rendered |
| `fits` | Each fitted field's sizes that fit, and the one chosen |
| `rules` | The complete rules: the measured ones a template requires (`image/overflow`, `image/glyph`, `image/fit`) decided, by format |
| `diagnostics` | What it found: each image's file against its declared size, its type and its transparency, and whether it would be upscaled in its region |

- **An image's region is the template's own element** bound to its field. A slot's content that names the field is
  never read as one.
- **It checks image files for the other roots too.** An Email, a Page or a Document has no layout to measure, so to
  check its image files in your own code, give an empty layout and the files:
  `checkLayout(template, values, { layout: { nodes: [], fits: [], diagnostics: [] }, files })`.
## Diagnostics

Every diagnostic has a `code`, a `path` into the values or the design, and a `message` that says what to change. One
on a bound node also names its `field`. Errors make a design invalid; warnings and notes don't.

### The values

| Code | What triggers it |
|------|------------------|
| `template/unknown-field` | A value for a field the template doesn't have. The message names the fields it has |
| `template/required` | A required field isn't given, or required text is empty or only spaces |
| `template/value` | A value its field refuses: the wrong type, text over its `maxLength` or outside its `pattern`, a block of an unknown type |
| `template/count` | A list or blocks outside its `min` and `max` |
| `template/format` | A format the template doesn't have; none named where it has several; or a design built at another size than its format's |

### Images

| Code | What triggers it |
|------|------------------|
| `template/asset-aspect` | The size given is outside the field's `aspect` |
| `template/asset-pixels` | The size given is under `minWidth` or `minHeight`, or the image would be upscaled in its region |
| `template/asset-type` | Its type isn't one the field `accepts`: by its name, or by its file |
| `template/asset-size` | The size given isn't its file's |
| `template/asset-alpha` | Its file's transparency isn't what `transparent` asks |
| `template/asset-unread` (note) | A rule only the file decides (`transparent`, a type its name doesn't give) wasn't decided: the file wasn't read |
| `template/asset-distorted` | A `contain` image is drawn at another aspect than its file's. Size it with `fitInside()` |
| `template/asset-cropped` | A `contain` image is a Layer's base (drawn as a cover), or a `cover` image loses more than `maxCrop` |
| `template/unbound` (warning) | An image field with rules that no node shows with `field` |

### The design and its bindings

| Code | What triggers it |
|------|------------------|
| `template/render` | The template's `render` threw |
| `template/root` | Its `render` returned another root than the template's, or another template |
| `template/unknown-binding` | A `field` that names no field with a value |
| `template/field-path` | A `field` that isn't a field's path (`headline`, `features[1]`, `stories[1].image`) |
| `field/dropped` (note) | A `field` inside a custom element's own render: it's left out |
| `template/not-root` | A template used beside or inside another node, or twice: a template is a design's root |
| `template/not-template` | `check(element)` given a design whose root isn't a template |

### Slots

| Code | What triggers it |
|------|------------------|
| `template/slot-element` | Content uses an element the slot doesn't allow, a root, an `Html` block, or its own definition of a custom element |
| `template/slot-style` | A style or a brand value the slot's `styles` doesn't take: a literal under `"theme"`, any style under `"none"` |
| `template/slot-tokens` | Content sets `tokens` or `theme` |
| `template/slot-attrs` | Content sets `attrs` |
| `template/slot-count` | A type's count is outside the slot's `count` |
| `template/slot-field` (note) | A `field` inside the content: it's the content's own |
| `template/slot-host` | The template places the slot nowhere, more than once, or in a node that isn't bound to it |
| `template/slot-unloaded` | A slot stored as its module, with no capture given in `fragments` |
| `template/slot-twice` | A slot's content given both in the values and in `fragments` |

### Rules over the result

| Code | What triggers it |
|------|------------------|
| `template/link-domain` | A link to a host that isn't in `links.domains` |
| `template/link-param` | A link without a parameter `links.params` requires |
| `template/link-scheme` | A link with a scheme that isn't in `links.schemes` |
| `template/link-relative` | A relative link |
| `template/link-tag` | A link with a sending service's tag: a note for review, or an error with `tags: "deny"`. Its host is checked by `links.domains` all the same, unless it's a tag |
| `template/image-domain` | An image that doesn't load from a host in `images.domains`: another host, a tag's, inline data or a relative address |
| `template/root-prop` | A root prop `rules.root` requires isn't set |
| `template/rule-not-run` | A required rule that didn't run: a note for a measured rule until the image is measured; an error if lint failed, or an output function was given the snapshot first |
| A lint rule's code, `image/overflow`, `layout/overflow`… | A finding of a required rule: an error, its message ending "(required by …)" |

### Fitted text and measuring

| Code | What triggers it |
|------|------------------|
| `image/fit` | Fitted text fits at none of its sizes. The message has the lines it takes and roughly how much to cut |
| `image/overflow` | Content runs past the Canvas |
| `image/glyph` | A character no font given has |
| `image/font`, `image/font-weight` | A family, or a weight, with no font file given |
| `fit/inline` | A run inside fitted text is in another size, font, weight or line height |
| `style/fit` | A `fontSize` written beside `fit`'s `sizes` |

`image/overflow`, `image/glyph` and the font codes are warnings for a design on its own, and errors where it's drawn strictly, as a design made from a template always is. The others are always errors.

### Defining a template

These are thrown by `template()` itself, when the module loads:

| Code | What triggers it |
|------|------------------|
| `template/spec` | A spec that isn't a template's: a bad `id` or `version`, a missing `example`, `fields` beside `design` |
| `template/field-name` | A field named `format`, `key`, `ref` or `children` |
| `template/block-type` | A block type with a field named `type` |
| `template/slot-allow` | A slot's `allow` isn't a list of elements or `"all"` |
| `template/rule-unavailable` | A required rule that lint doesn't have, that's off as lint is configured, or that doesn't run on the template's root |
| `template/plugin` | A plugin in `rules.plugins.other` that's a Promise: await it first |

An [annotated template](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots#annotated-templates)'s markers have their own:

| Code | What triggers it |
|------|------------------|
| `template/inline-kind` | A marker for a field that isn't text, a link, an image or a slot |
| `template/inline-target` | A marker that isn't on a built-in element |
| `template/inline-content` | A text marker's node holds something other than one string |
| `template/inline-unplaced` | A field in `open` whose marker isn't in `design` |
| `template/inline-unlisted` | A marker in `design` that isn't named in `open` |
| `template/inline-twice` | One marker given two names |
| `template/inline-nested` | A marker inside a slot's host, where the slot's content replaces it |
| `template/inline-hidden` | A marker inside the render of a function or a custom element of your own |

### Values files

| Code | What triggers it |
|------|------------------|
| `template/values-file` | A file that isn't `{ version: 1, template: { module, id, version }, values, … }` |
| `template/id` | A file made for another template |
| `template/version` | A file made with a newer version; a new major with no migration from the file's; or a migration that threw |
| `template/upgraded` (note) | A file made with an older version, read with this one |
| `template/changed` (warning) | The template's module changed under the same version (the command line) |
| `template/asset-changed` (warning) | A file a design recorded changed under the same name (the command line) |

### Snapshots and captured content

| Code | What triggers it |
|------|------------------|
| `jsx/value` | A value that isn't plain data: a function, a class instance |
| `jsx/fragment` | A capture that isn't one: its kind, its version, a node's keys, more than 64 levels deep or 8 MB |
| `jsx/slot-mark` | `slotMark()` used outside a snapshot |
| `builder/snapshot`, `builder/template` | `toDesign()` given a snapshot or a template design: it takes a design's element (`design(values)`) |

The command line's own codes (`cli/…`, `extract/…`) are on [Templates in the command line](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/cli#diagnostics).

---

# Templates in the command line

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/cli

How the [`hyper-elements` command](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/cli) works with templates. [Template examples](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/examples)
runs these commands on real templates, with what each writes.

Every command exits `0` when it's done, `1` when a design has errors, and `2` when it couldn't run at all: a wrong
option, a missing package. [JSON and exit codes](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/cli#json-and-exit-codes) has the rest.

## The commands

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `describe templates/launch-graphic.tsx` | What a template takes: its formats, fields, image regions and rules. `--json` has all of it |
| `design new <template> -o <name.values.json>` | Makes a design from a template: a values file |
| `design set <name.values.json> field=value` | Changes values in a design; the rest stays as it was |
| `check <design>` | Checks a design: its values, its images against their files, fitted text, each format |
| `render <design>` | Checks it the same way, then writes its output: one file per format |
| `check <template>` | Checks a template module with its example in every format: a template's CI |
| `template extract <design> --id … --field … -o <template>` | Makes a template from a design a person approved |

A design is a values file (`name.values.json`) or a TSX file whose root is a template. Both are checked the same way.

## Values files

A values file names its template's module, the formats wanted and the values:

```bash
npx hyper-elements design new templates/launch-graphic.tsx -o designs/orbit.values.json \
  --values brief.json --set artwork=@art/shapes.png --source artwork=source.json
npx hyper-elements design set designs/orbit.values.json launchDate=2026-12-10
```

| You give | It's read as |
|----------|--------------|
| `--values brief.json` | The values to start from (`design new`) |
| `--set field=value`, or `field=value` after the file (`design set`) | JSON where it parses, else text. A nested value goes by its path: `customer.name=Northwind`, `lines[2].price=30`, `features[0]=…` |
| `field=@path/to/image.png` | An image file: its size is read from it, and its hash goes in the file's `assets` |
| `field=@path/to/body.tsx` | A slot's content, stored as its module |
| `--source field=source.json` | Where an image came from, recorded beside its hash: a JSON object with a `kind` (`"supplied"`, `"generated"`, `"stock"` or your own) and whatever else you keep, such as a provider, a model and a prompt, or a license |
| `--draft` | Writes the file even where values are missing, with `"draft": true` and what's `missing` |

- **A value the template refuses exits `1`**, and the file stays as it was.
- **`design new` lists every format the template has.** To render fewer, take one out of the file's `formats`.
- **`design set` first brings the file up to the template's current version:** its migrations run, for a draft too.
  So a set can repair a file whose values the template refuses. A file of another template, or of a newer version, is
  left alone.
- **A draft isn't rendered** (`cli/draft`) until a `design set` completes it.
- **An image's entry follows its file.** Moved to another field, it keeps its hash and source. Changed under the same
  name, it has no source until one is given (`template/asset-changed`). `check` lists an image with no source under
  `review`.

### Paths

| A path | Is relative to |
|--------|----------------|
| The template's module, in a values file | The values file (or it's a package specifier, kept as given) |
| A template's own files: its logo, its fonts, its example's pictures | The template's module |
| A Canvas's or a Document's image, in a design | The design: its values file or its TSX file. The command line reads it to draw it |
| An Email's or a Page's image `src` | Nothing: it's written into the HTML as it's given (a URL, a service's tag such as `{{logo_url}}`, `cid:`). Where it's a file's path, the file is read relative to the design, only to check it |
| A slot's module | The values file |

## Checking and rendering

`render`, `check`, `inspect` and `outline` run a values file once per format it lists. Each format has its own line
(`templateFormat` with `--json`) and its own file, `<name>.<format>.<ext>`.

| Flag | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `--template-format square` | Runs one of the template's formats |
| `--format svg` | The file type of a Canvas's image (`png` or `svg`), as for any Canvas. Not a template's format |
| `--scale 2` | Pixels per px, in place of the format's own scale |
| `--require-template [id]` | Fails every input that isn't a design a template checked, or is one of another template |
| `--props file.json` | A TSX design's props, as for any design |

What's checked, in order:

1. **The values**, by the template: a wrong one is a `template/…` error.
2. **The design**, as any design is, with lint and the email client checks where they apply.
3. **A Canvas, measured** at the scale it's rendered at, strict: a font that isn't given fails, fitted text is sized,
   and each image is checked against its region and its file.
4. **Image files, for the other roots too:** an image that's a file beside the design is read and checked for its
   type, its transparency and the size it's given as. One that isn't read (a URL) leaves those undecided, said as
   `template/asset-unread`.

`check --json` adds `fits`, `regions` (each image's box and the pixels it needs), `rules` and `review` (what a
reviewer looks at by eye, which never fails a run). `render` checks the same, and writes nothing for a format that
fails.

`outline` and `--stdout` take one input, so a file of two formats needs `--template-format`. A template with formats
checks a file that lists none as `template/format`.

## TSX template designs

A design can be TSX with the template as its root:

```tsx
import { Column, Heading, Text } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import Newsletter from "../templates/newsletter";

export default () => <Newsletter subject="What's new in June" body={<Column><Heading level={2}>Faster exports</Heading><Text>…</Text></Column>} />;
```

The command line runs the design file only far enough to read which template it uses and the props it gives it. Then
it checks and renders those as it does a values file, one output per format. Running it is running code:
[a TSX design is reviewed as code](#what-that-guarantees-and-what-it-doesnt).

- It's rendered with the props any design gets: `--props file.json`, else the sample props its file gives
  ([`PreviewProps`](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/cli)).
- A design whose template isn't among its own imports, or whose props aren't data (a function), is
  `cli/template-design`.
- `design new <template> --from designs/june.tsx -o june.values.json` writes its values file.

## Slots stored as modules

A values file's slot can be its module, relative to the file:

```bash
npx hyper-elements design set designs/june.values.json body=@designs/_slots/june.body.tsx
```

[A slot module](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/slots#a-slot-stored-as-data) is a component that renders the content. It runs
in a process of its own, which can reply only with what it rendered. It's still code, with that process's access to
the machine: [review it as code](#what-that-guarantees-and-what-it-doesnt). One that throws, sends anything
else, sends more than 8 MB or exits first is `cli/slot-module` (exit `1`), and nothing is written. Its hash is kept
in `assets`, as an image's is.

Keep slot modules in a folder whose name starts with `_` (`designs/_slots/june.body.tsx`) where you check or render a
whole folder: a folder run takes every module with a default export for a design.

## Trusted templates

A values file names its own template, and so does a TSX design. Without a list, a design could name any template:
one somebody wrote to let anything through. So list the templates a project's designs may use, in the nearest
`package.json`:

```json
{ "hyperElements": { "templates": ["templates/**", "@acme/brand-templates"] } }
```

Paths and globs are relative to it; a name is a package.

| With the list | What happens |
|---------------|--------------|
| A template outside it | `cli/template-untrusted`, exit `1` |
| A template inside it | Loaded in a process that refuses anything it imports outside the list and your installed packages: statically, dynamically or with `require()`, before it runs, naming who imported it |
| A file in a listed folder that isn't a template (a design someone kept there) | Runs as any design does |
| A `package.json` that can't be read as JSON | The run stops, exit `2`: it can't say there's no list |
| On Bun | Bun's plugins can't see every load, so a project with the list runs its templates on Node (exit `2` on Bun) |

Without the list, templates load as any design does, with `"trusted": false` and a `cli/template-untrusted` warning.

In CI, `--require-template` on `check` and `render` fails anything a template didn't check:

```bash
npx hyper-elements check designs/ --require-template acme.Newsletter
```

### What that guarantees, and what it doesn't

`--require-template` checks what a design gives its template. It doesn't check what a design's code does.

| A design that is | Is | Take it from an agent, or unreviewed? |
|------------------|----|----------------------------------------|
| A values file with no slot module | Data. Nothing in it runs | Yes. `--require-template` then means the design is what the template checked |
| A TSX design | Code. The command line runs it to read its props, before the template checks anything | No: review it as you review any code |
| A values file with a slot module | Data that names code. The module runs to render the slot's content | No: review the module |

Code that runs can do what its process can: read and write files, the template's among them. A TSX design could
change a trusted template for the length of a run and put it back, and the run would pass. The list and the guard
stop a template from loading code outside the list; they don't stop a design's own code.

So for agents, and for designs nobody reviews, use templates whose open parts are data (fields and blocks), filled as
values files. Review TSX designs and slot modules like the rest of your code.

A template guarantees what it checks, not who may edit it. Commit templates and review changes to them (with
CODEOWNERS, for example), and don't give whatever fills them write access to the templates folder.

## A template from an existing design

A design a person approved can become a template. Give each part that changes an `id`, then extract it:

```bash
npx hyper-elements template extract designs/orbit.tsx --id acme.LaunchGraphic \
  --field headline --field features --field launchDate --field artwork -o templates/launch-graphic.tsx
```

| In the design | In the template |
|---------------|-----------------|
| A literal text child of the node with that `id` | A `prop.text` field, the literal its `example` |
| An Image's literal `src={{ src, width, height }}` | A `field.image`, the literal its `example` |
| Siblings with ids `features-0`, `features-1`, … | One `prop.list` |
| The node itself | Keeps its `id`, and gains `field` |
| The rest of the file: its theme, variants and components | As written, with relative imports and `src` paths rewritten for the template's folder |

It writes a template with `fields`, an `example` and a `render`, at version `0.1.0`. A value that isn't a literal is
`extract/not-literal`, with its line and column, and nothing is written. Then add the template's rules and formats,
set its `version`, and `check` it.

## Diagnostics

The template's own diagnostics (`template/…`) are on [Rules, checks and diagnostics](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/templates/rules#diagnostics).
These are the command line's:

| Code | What triggers it | Exit |
|------|------------------|------|
| `cli/values-file` | A values file that isn't one: not JSON, the wrong shape, a template module that isn't found or is given by an absolute path | `1` |
| `cli/template-format` | A format the file or the template doesn't have; or `outline` or `--stdout` given more than one | `1` or `2` |
| `cli/draft` | `render` of a draft | `1` |
| `cli/render-template` | `render` of a template module: render a design made from it | `2` |
| `cli/not-a-template-module` | A values file's module whose default export isn't a template | `1` |
| `cli/template-design` | A TSX design whose template can't be found among its imports, or whose props aren't data | `1` |
| `cli/slot-module` | A slot's module that throws, replies with anything but its capture, or exits first | `1` |
| `cli/template-untrusted` | A template outside the trusted list (an error), or loaded with no list (a warning) | `1` |
| `cli/template-required` | With `--require-template`, an input no template checked, or one of another template | `1` |
| `cli/engine-missing` | A Canvas template's design, where the image engines aren't installed | `2` |
| `cli/elements-version` | A template or a values file, with an `@hyper-elements/react` from before templates | `2` |
| `extract/not-literal` | A field's value that isn't a literal | `1` |
| `extract/no-id` | No element in the design has the `id` a `--field` names | `1` |
| `extract/props` | A design that takes props | `1` |
