The Hyper Elements project's `CLAUDE.md` also imported the package's guide, [as we tell you to set it up](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/guides/ai-agents). The MJML project compiled `emails/email.mjml` with MJML's defaults.

## What it doesn't show

- One agent and one model. Other agents and models may differ.
- Short, fully specified emails. A vague brief or a long email may change the picture.
- Hyper Elements 0.3, MJML 5.4.1 and React Email components 1.0.12.

## Image results

Five briefs, four runs per brief per approach: **60 valid, isolated runs**, all of which reached a passing image.

[![Image agent benchmark comparing Hyper Elements, Playwright and Canvas 2D on median time, output tokens and first-check passes. Full results follow in the table.](https://www.hyperelements.dev/img/hyper-elements-image-benchmark.svg)](https://www.hyperelements.dev/img/hyper-elements-image-benchmark.svg "Open the image benchmark chart at full size")

| | Hyper Elements | Playwright | Canvas 2D |
|---|---|---|---|
| Median time to a passing image | **76s** | 91s | 125s |
| Median output tokens | **5,096** | 6,846 | 9,132 |
| Passed the checks the first time they ran | **17 of 20** | 14 of 20 | 16 of 20 |

- **Against Canvas 2D:** 1.65× faster and 1.8× fewer output tokens at the median. Hyper Elements was faster in 57 of 80 pairings within a brief (one-sided Mann–Whitney, p = 0.003); the output-token comparison also favored Hyper Elements (p = 0.002).
- **Against Playwright:** a lower overall median, but no clear speed advantage within briefs (40 of 80 pairings, p = 0.35). Playwright was faster on the blog and launch cards; Hyper Elements was faster on the podcast, quote and event briefs.
- **First-check passes:** 17 of 20 with Hyper Elements, 14 of 20 with Playwright and 16 of 20 with Canvas 2D. Every run eventually passed.

### The images

Each brief specifies the exact copy, dimensions, colors, fonts and images. All approaches use the same local fonts and image files, with no network access.

| Brief | Output | What it checks |
|---|---|---|
| Blog post OG card | 1200 × 630 | Title, author and logo placement |
| Product launch card | 1200 × 630 | Background image, headline and pill |
| Conference banner | 1500 × 500 | Wide layout, event details and safe margins |
| Podcast episode card | 1080 × 1080 | Square layout and rounded artwork |
| Quote card | 1200 × 675 | Lora italic, attribution and text wrapping |

### Image checks and setup

Each approach received the same instructions: write a renderer that returns PNG bytes. Hyper Elements used `Canvas` and `renderImage()` (Satori and resvg); Playwright took a Chromium screenshot of HTML; Canvas 2D drew with `@napi-rs/canvas`.

The shared checker reads a rendering trace to verify exact text, font files, weight, style, size and color. It also checks the PNG's dimensions, background and image placement, and uses offline OCR to check readable text, safe margins, wrapping, alignment and overlaps. Each run starts in an isolated directory; an audit rejects runs that reach outside it.

These results use Hyper Elements 0.3.0, Playwright 1.60.0 and `@napi-rs/canvas` 1.0.13. They measure one agent and model on five fully specified images. They measure the agent's work through a passing result, including repairs, rather than render speed alone.

The chart uses the [final 60-run batch](https://github.com/hyper-elements/hyper-elements/blob/main/benchmark/results/2026-11-08b-image-sonnet.jsonl). It excludes the earlier batch, which was rerun after the kit instructions and TypeScript import settings were made consistent. See the [image benchmark notes](https://github.com/hyper-elements/hyper-elements/tree/main/benchmark#image-2026-11-08-results2026-11-08b-image-sonnetjsonl) for the per-brief results and rerun details.

The harness, the briefs, the checks and every run's numbers are in the repository's [`benchmark/`](https://github.com/hyper-elements/hyper-elements/tree/main/benchmark) folder. Run it yourself with your own agent.

---

# Visual editing

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/guides/visual-editor

You or an agent writes the design in code. Someone else changes the copy in a visual editor. You don't maintain two versions, and you don't hand-build the builder's design JSON.

`@hyper-elements/react/builder` connects your designs to Unlayer's builder, the drag-and-drop email and page editor:

- `toDesign(element)` writes a design as a builder design, the builder's design JSON, for its `loadDesign()`.
- `fromDesign(design, options)` reads a builder design back as a design: an element to render, and its JSX source.

Rendering needs no Unlayer account or API key. The builder is Unlayer's product, with its own project setup.

## Design to builder design

```tsx
import { mkdir, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { toDesign } from "@hyper-elements/react/builder";
import { Email, Text } from "@hyper-elements/react";

const { design, report } = toDesign(
  <Email width={600}>
    <Text>Welcome to your new workspace.</Text>
  </Email>
);
for (const line of report) console.warn(line);
await mkdir("output", { recursive: true });
await writeFile("output/design.json", JSON.stringify(design, null, 2));
```

`design` is a serializable object with `body`, `counters` and `schemaVersion`. It holds the builder's structure, not HTML, and no Elements data. Keep the schema version and counters it writes.

`toDesign()` is synchronous. It takes an `Email`, a `Page` or a `Document`. A `Canvas` has no builder design. It renders the design once with React, as `render()` does, so hooks, Context, Fragments and your own components work, at the root too.

## The report

`report` lists what the builder can't hold as it is, one line each, with the path to the block. It's empty when everything maps to a builder tool. A `Table` in an `Email` with a line between its rows (`rowBorder`), which the builder's table can't draw, for example:

```text
root.children[1]: the builder's table doesn't draw it as it is (a line between rows only): it's an HTML block of its own markup in the builder (it can be moved, not edited)
```

Read the report before you promise an editor user that a block is editable.

## What the builder holds

The builder holds what its tools can. Two things happen to the rest:

- **Hidden properties.** A style or prop a tool has no field for is a hidden property of that tool. It's kept in the builder design under its own name and drawn by Elements, but the builder shows no control for it yet.
- **HTML blocks.** What no tool shows (a `Layer`, an `Svg`, a box nested in a column, your own `defineElement()`) goes in as an HTML block of its rendered markup. An editor user can move it, not edit it. In a `Document`, the builder keeps an HTML block but doesn't draw or export it, so it isn't in the builder's PDF. The report names each one.
- **Tables.** A `Table` is the builder's table: its header and footer rows, each cell's words and each column's share, what its rows share (text styles, background, padding) and each cell's own. The builder draws one border around every cell and has no cells across columns, no table width and no phone values. In an `Email` or a `Page`, a table the builder would draw otherwise (a line between rows only, a cell spanning columns, a border around the table, a width, a column of a fixed width) stays an HTML block, which draws it exactly. In a `Document`, where the builder doesn't draw an HTML block, it's the builder's table all the same: a line between rows is drawn above the first row and below the last too, and a cell spanning columns is a cell for each column. A table with an image in a cell, or a row, a cell or words in a cell hidden on phones or desktops, stays an HTML block. The report says each. `fromDesign()` reads a table back as a `Table`, one made in the builder too.

Two smaller details: a line height goes into the builder's field as a whole percentage, as browsers draw it, so `24px` at 13px becomes `185%`, a twentieth of a pixel taller there. The builder has no page numbers yet, so a `PageNumber` goes in as its token, which the editor's PDF prints as it is. The report says so.

## Load it in the builder

Create the editor, load the builder design when it's ready, and export when the user is done:

```html
<div id="editor" style="height: 80vh"></div>
<script src="https://editor.unlayer.com/embed.js"></script>
<script>
  const editor = unlayer.createEditor({
    id: "editor",
    displayMode: "email",
    // Add your projectId and allowed domain for your deployed integration.
  });
  editor.addEventListener("editor:ready", async () => {
    const response = await fetch("./output/design.json");
    editor.loadDesign(await response.json());
  });
  function save() {
    editor.exportHtml(({ design, html }) => {
      // Store `design` in your application. Load it next time to keep the edits.
    });
  }
</script>
```

Match the editor's `displayMode` to the design's root: `email` for an `Email`, `web` for a `Page`, `document` for a `Document`. Which tools and features the editor offers depends on its version and your project's configuration. Unlayer's docs cover [installing the editor](https://docs.unlayer.com/builder/installation) and [loading and saving designs](https://docs.unlayer.com/builder/load-and-save-designs).

> **Warning:** Once an editor user has changed a builder design, store their latest JSON and load that. Regenerating the builder design from your React source and reloading it overwrites their changes. Keep the design's source and the saved builder designs as separate records.

## Builder design back to a design

```tsx
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { fromDesign } from "@hyper-elements/react/builder";
import { render } from "@hyper-elements/react";

const saved = JSON.parse(await readFile("edited.design.json", "utf8"));
const { element, code, report } = fromDesign(saved, { displayMode: "email" });
const { html, text } = await render(element);
```

- `element` renders the builder design. `render(element)` gives HTML and a plain-text body that match the edits, ready to [send](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/guides/sending).
- `code` is the same design as JSX in the new elements.
- `report` lists what the design can't hold.

Pass the `displayMode` the builder design was made in: `email` gives an `Email`, `web` a `Page`, `document` a `Document`. Without one, a builder design with a header, a footer or a page break becomes a `Document`, any other an `Email`. `name` sets the component's name in `code`. `fromDesign()` reads builder designs made by `toDesign()`, edited in the builder, or made there from scratch. The builder's own HTML blocks come back as `Html` blocks.

### What comes back

The builder design as it stands, with its sample values. A builder design holds content and settings, not code, so the original's props, loops, conditions, hooks and event handlers don't come back.

What the builder can't arrange comes back with the same look, but flatter:

- a `Section` around several `Row`s comes back as a `Section` each;
- a box's padding comes back on its blocks;
- a `Grid` comes back as `Row`s of `Column`s.

The space between blocks comes back as padding too. A `Column` with `gap: 16` comes back like this, drawn the same:

```tsx
<Column style={{ padding: 32, backgroundColor: "#ffffff" }}>
  <Heading style={{ fontSize: 24 }}>{"Welcome, "}<MergeTag name="first_name" /></Heading>
  <Text style={{ padding: [16, 0, 0, 0] }}>Your Pro workspace is ready.</Text>
</Column>
```

### Untrusted builder designs: `toSafeHtml`

A builder design's markup comes back as it is. If your builder designs can hold content you don't trust, pass your sanitizer as `toSafeHtml`, a function from an HTML string to a safe one. Every builder HTML block's markup, and every text's before it's read, goes through it:

```tsx
const { element } = fromDesign(saved, { displayMode: "email", toSafeHtml });
```

## Limits

- A component that is async or suspends makes `toDesign()` throw, as it makes `render()` reject. Fetch data before you build the tree.
- Plain markup among the elements (a `<div>`, a `<b>`) makes `toDesign()` throw too. Use the elements, or an `Html` block for raw HTML, which the editor edits as HTML.
- Don't construct or guess a builder design's JSON by hand. Generate it with `toDesign()`.

---

# From React Email

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/migrate/react-email

You don't rewrite your React Email templates by hand. One command converts them, keeps their props, loops and conditions, and then checks each migrated template against its original, so you know what changed before you ship it.

```bash
npx @hyper-elements/migrate emails           # converts and checks your templates, and writes nothing
npx @hyper-elements/migrate emails --write   # then replaces them (committed in git first, so git can undo it)
```

Still weighing a React Email alternative? [Hyper Elements vs React Email](https://www.hyperelements.dev/compare/react-email) compares the two side by side.

Run it from your project folder, with Node.js 20.6 or later. It uses your project's React, React Email and `tsconfig` paths.

## What it converts

Each template becomes the elements from `@hyper-elements/react`, with its styles in `style={{ }}`:

| React Email | Hyper Elements |
|---|---|
| `Text` | `Text` |
| `Section`, `Row`, `Column` | `Section`, `Row`, `Column` |
| `Button` | `Button` |
| `Container` width | `Email` `width` |
| `Img` | `Image`, with its file's size in `src={{ src, width, height }}` |
| `Hr` | `Divider` |
| `Preview` | `Email` `previewText` |
| Margins | Padding on the blocks |
| Tailwind classes and inline styles | `style={{ }}` |

- **Tailwind** classes are resolved with React Email's own Tailwind and your template's config, then become styles.
- **Your own components** that a template uses, from the same file or your other files (a shared `Layout`, a `Footer`, also through an `index.ts` that re-exports them), are inlined, so their markup converts too.
- **Anything with no equivalent** is kept as an `Html` block that renders exactly as before. The block is marked `TODO(convert)` in the migrated template.
- **Default exports** wrapped in `memo` or `forwardRef` work, nested wrappers included. A template that calls hooks (`useMemo`, `useId`) migrates like any other.
- **Language and direction:** the document's `lang` and `dir` become `Email`'s `lang` and `dir` props.

JavaScript templates keep JavaScript. A `.js` file with JSX can't be loaded: rename it to `.jsx`.

## How it checks the result

The goal is an editable design with the same content, not pixel parity. The original and the migrated template are rendered with the template's `PreviewProps`, then again with each boolean prop flipped, and compared in two parts.

### Content must match

- every word the original renders, including numbers with their separators, signs, currency symbols and percentages, in the same order;
- every link, image and image `alt` text;
- no new words, links or images;
- the same on a phone (375px), and on wider screens where a rule targets them (Tailwind's `md:`, `lg:`);
- the same in dark mode, where either side has a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` rule (a logo or text swapped for dark mode);
- whether content shows, including content the original shows or hides by its props (`isGift && "hidden"`), and words CSS adds or hides (`::before` content, an ellipsis, a line clamp, a clipping `overflow`);
- every block reaching the visual editor.

Anything the converter can't map is kept as HTML, so content that differs is a converter bug. The template is still written, flagged `✗`, and the run exits with `2`. Please report it.

### How it looks is listed

At a desktop width (700px), each word's size, bold, italics, letter case, underline, color, the background behind it and a link's target; where each line of text sits across the page (a column stacked into one, a block moved to the other side); and CSS the check doesn't model that can change how words show (`white-space`, letter spacing, a transform, a text shadow, right-to-left text), unless both sides have the same. A difference here is listed under "looks different", for you to fix in the editor. The run still exits `0`.

The check fails closed: when it can't read something on one side (a selector, a condition, a value), it says so, naming the rule, instead of passing it.

### What isn't verified

Vertical spacing, exact positions (under about 120px), where images sit and an image's `srcset`, fonts as drawn, borders, corners and outer shadows, styles in dark mode (what shows there is compared), hover, and how each email client renders.

Code paths your `PreviewProps` don't reach (a loop over an empty preview array, a condition on a non-boolean prop) are converted but not verified. Extend `PreviewProps` to cover them.

## The report

```text
✓ emails/welcome.tsx: 100% editable, 1 kind of difference (image border radius dropped)
✓ emails/comment.tsx: 100% editable
    looks different: couldn't verify: the look of "Alex", "can", "you" (`white-space: pre-wrap`, a style the check doesn't verify)
- emails/components/layout.tsx: skipped (no default-exported component)

2 templates: 2 migrated and checked (1 looks different: see above). 1 other file skipped (see above). 2 written.
```

For each template:

- **Editable**: the share of content that became blocks you can edit in the visual editor. The rest is kept as HTML blocks that render exactly as before.
- **Differences**: what Hyper Elements can't express, and how it was approximated.
- **What the migration did**: changes that don't affect the look (a component inlined, a conditional `className` split into one element per class list).

Files that aren't templates (shared components, helpers, a framework's routes) are listed after the templates as skipped, with why. Write the report to a file with `--report`.

## Options

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--write` | Replace each template with its migrated version. Only templates git can restore: committed, with no changes since. |
| `--out <dir>` | Write migrated templates to `<dir>` instead, keeping the folder layout. Relative imports still resolve. |
| `--design` | Also write the builder design, `<name>.design.json`, next to each template, for the visual editor's `loadDesign()`. Text props shown as given become merge tags (`{{name}}`). |
| `--no-merge-tags` | Keep the `PreviewProps` values in the builder design instead of merge tags. |
| `--report <file>` | Write the migration report: JSON for a `.json` file, Markdown for any other. |
| `--strict` | Fail a template with any difference, in its content, its look, or a style the migration couldn't keep, and don't write it. |
| `--force` | With `--strict`, write templates the check fails anyway. |
| `--overwrite` | Replace files already at a destination that this run didn't produce: what an earlier run wrote in an `--out` folder (not once it's edited), or files git can restore. |
| `--allow-dirty` | Replace files git can't restore (changed since the last commit, not committed, or not in a repository), with `--write` or `--overwrite`. |
| `--from <source>` | `react-email` (the default), or `unlayer-elements` to [move Unlayer Elements templates](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/migrate/unlayer-elements). |
| `-h`, `--help` | Show the help. |
| `-v`, `--version` | Show the version. |

Without `--write` or `--out`, nothing is written. Run it once to read the report, then again with `--write`.

### Safe writes

`--write` replaces templates in place, so before running anything it checks that git can give each one back. A template with uncommitted changes, one that isn't committed, or one outside a git repository stops the run with exit `1`, naming them. Commit first, and git can undo the migration. `--out <dir>` writes copies and doesn't need git. `--allow-dirty` replaces templates anyway.

All templates are converted and checked before any output is written. A template edited while the run converts it isn't replaced: it fails, and your edit stays. A run stopped with Ctrl-C cleans up after itself. One killed outright (`kill -9`) can leave a temporary copy next to a template, a dot-file named after it, safe to delete.

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `0` | Every template converted with the same content. What looks different is listed. |
| `1` | A usage error, no templates found, a template left unchecked because a file that renders it isn't migrated (a preview around it: migrate it with `--out`), a Node.js older than 20.6, an installed `@hyper-elements/react` this version doesn't support, or a `--write` blocked by files git can't restore. |
| `2` | A template failed to convert, its content differs (with `--strict`, anything differs), a file couldn't be read, or the run couldn't go on. |

A run never ends with `0` without checking what it was given. That makes it safe in CI: templates already migrated are skipped, so running it again after `--write` passes.

## Check a template you migrated yourself

```bash
npx @hyper-elements/migrate compare emails/welcome.tsx emails/welcome.elements.tsx
```

`compare` renders both with the original's `PreviewProps`, then with each true/false prop flipped, and checks the HTML and the builder design: every word, link, image and `alt` text is still there, no new words appear, and the visual editor gets every block. What looks different is listed. Exit `0` when the content is the same, `2` with missing or extra content (with `--strict`, with any difference).

Use it after you convert a `TODO(convert)` block by hand: replace it with the new elements, then run `compare` against the original (from git, if `--write` replaced it).

## How well it works

Measured on 106 real templates: 71 of React Email's own demo and example emails, 25 community templates from MIT repositories, and 10 written by agents. The codemod migrates your source; the runtime mode converts what a template renders, as `convertReactEmail()` does.

| | Codemod | Runtime |
|---|---|---|
| Converted | 106 of 106 | 106 of 106 |
| Type-check | 106 of 106 | 106 of 106 |
| Lose content | 0 | 0 |
| Problems with a boolean prop flipped | 0 | 0 |
| Blocks the editor skips | 0 | 0 |
| Editable, on average | 98.4% | 98.4% |
| Fully editable | 96 | 97 |
| Words moved on desktop (median) | 0% | 0% |

On desktop, in 105 of 106 templates at most a quarter of the words sit somewhere else, and the median is none. The one outlier sets no font, so the browser shows serif where Hyper Elements uses its sans-serif default. No conversion has a style difference on desktop. Three have one on phones: text the converter makes smaller so its words fit.

## What changes

The report lists every difference for each template. The common ones:

- **Phones.** React Email's rows are tables and never stack, so columns stay side by side, unless the template stacks them (`mobile:!block`). Side by side, they keep their share of the row, so fixed widths and images scale down with it.
- **Phone styles** become phone settings for padding, margins, font size, line height, alignment and hiding. Others (a color, font weight, letter spacing) and hover styles have no equivalent. Phone settings use a 480px breakpoint, so a source query such as `max-width: 600px` differs between 481px and 600px.
- **Column vertical alignment.** A React Email `Column` is a `<td>`, centered vertically by default. Email columns here sit at the top. It shows only next to a taller column.
- **Shadows, gradients, transforms.** A box's outer shadow is dropped and a gradient background becomes its first color. A transform, a text shadow or an inset shadow changes how text shows, so a template with one is listed as looking different.
- **Image border radius** is dropped.
- **Attributes** a block has no place for (`id`, `title`, `role`, `aria-*`).
- **A box that shrinks to fit its content** (`w-fit` around text) is as wide as its parent.
- **Text without a font family** uses the default font rather than the browser's.

## A template that can't be converted

A template that can't be written in the elements at all fails: nothing is written for it, the report says why, and the run exits `2`. Rewrite that part by hand, then check it against the React Email original with `npx @hyper-elements/migrate compare <original> <migrated>`.

## After migrating

Install the package, since the migrated templates import it:

```bash
npm install @hyper-elements/react@^0.5.0
```

When a run writes templates where it isn't installed, it ends with the install command for your package manager (npm, pnpm, yarn or bun, by your lockfile).

```tsx
import { render } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import { toDesign } from "@hyper-elements/react/builder";
import Welcome from "./emails/welcome";

const element = <Welcome name="Alex" />;
const { html, text } = await render(element); // send html with any provider, with text as the text part
const { design } = toDesign(element);         // open in the visual editor with loadDesign()
```

You can remove React Email once no file imports it. After `--write`, the run lists the files that still import it, and the project files that still use a migrated template with React Email's `render()`: render those with `render()` from `@hyper-elements/react` instead. Templates with blocks kept as HTML still import React Email components for those blocks; the report lists them.

## Open React Email templates in Unlayer's builder

`--design` makes any React Email template editable in Unlayer's visual builder, without changing your source:

```bash
npx @hyper-elements/migrate emails --out unlayer --design --report unlayer/report.json
```

```js
editor.loadDesign(await fetch("/unlayer/welcome.design.json").then((r) => r.json()));
```

Web fonts aren't part of the builder design: the editor loads and exports a web font only when it's registered when the editor is created. The JSON report lists each template's fonts in that shape:

```js
const report = await fetch("/unlayer/report.json").then((r) => r.json());
const customFonts = report.flatMap((result) => result.fonts ?? []);
const editor = unlayer.createEditor({ id: "editor", displayMode: "email", fonts: { showDefaultFonts: true, customFonts } });
```

## From code

Use the converter from an agent, a build step or a server:

```bash
npm install @hyper-elements/migrate
```

```ts
import { convertReactEmail, NewComponentsError } from "@hyper-elements/migrate/react-email";
import Welcome from "./emails/welcome";

const conversion = await convertReactEmail(Welcome); // rendered with its PreviewProps, and checked against it
const tsx = conversion.code;                  // the design in the elements
const html = await conversion.html();
const design = conversion.design();           // open in the visual editor with loadDesign()
const customFonts = conversion.editorFonts(); // register when creating the editor: fonts: { customFonts }
conversion.report.missingText;                // [] when nothing was lost
```

`convertReactEmail()` converts what a template renders: loops and conditions become the content they produced (the CLI keeps them). Where that can't be written in the elements, it throws a `NewComponentsError`, whose `reason` says why.

> **Warning:** The command runs your templates to check them: a template's module code runs, and its component renders, as React Email's preview does. Run it only on code you trust. It makes no network requests.

---

# From Unlayer Elements

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/migrate/unlayer-elements

Hyper Elements is a new package. It doesn't include the components of Unlayer Elements, `@unlayer/react-elements` (`ColumnLayouts`, `html` props, `renderToHtml()`), so templates written with them have to move, and nothing changes until they do. A codemod rewrites them with the new elements. It rewrites the imports and the JSX, and nothing else: your props, loops, conditions, helpers and constants stay as they are.

A template uses the old components or the new elements, never both. Move a template whole.

## Run the codemod

```bash
npx @hyper-elements/migrate src/emails --from unlayer-elements                  # lists what it would change
npx @hyper-elements/migrate src/emails/welcome.tsx --from unlayer-elements > welcome.next.tsx   # prints one template
npx @hyper-elements/migrate src/emails --from unlayer-elements --write          # replaces them (only files git can restore)
```

Then install the new package, and remove the old one once nothing imports it. What the codemod keeps of the old package's API (`renderToHtml()`, say) stays imported from it, and it's listed for you to replace:

```bash
npm install @hyper-elements/react
npm uninstall @unlayer/react-elements
```

Each migrated template starts with the line `// Migrated from Unlayer Elements by @hyper-elements/migrate.`, so a second run changes nothing.

`--write` only replaces templates git can restore, so commit first. `--allow-dirty` skips that check. `--report notes.md` (or `.json`) writes what the codemod noted for each template.

JSX inside expressions (`items.map(...)`, `cond && ...`) is rewritten in place. A `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs` or `.cjs` template gets JavaScript, a `.ts` or `.tsx` one TypeScript.

### Which files it touches

Templates are the files that import Unlayer Elements' components, directly or through your own modules that pass them on (an index with `export { Email } from ...` or `export *` from it, followed as your `tsconfig` resolves it). Other files, such as one that only calls `renderToHtml()` or that index itself, are left as they are and aren't listed.

A namespace re-export (`export * as E from ...`) isn't followed: a template that uses one fails, naming the file. A template whose root is chosen at run time (`const Root = web ? Page : Email`) stays as it was, with a note: write it with one root.

### From code

```ts
import { migrateElements } from "@hyper-elements/migrate/elements";

const { code, report } = await migrateElements(source);
```

A module that comes back as it was because it's already on the new elements has `current: true`.

## Before and after

```tsx
// Before
<Email>
  <Row layout={ColumnLayouts.TwoEqual} backgroundColor="#ffffff">
    <Column>
      <Heading headingType="h1">Welcome, {name}</Heading>
      <Paragraph html="Your workspace is <b>ready</b>." />
    </Column>
    <Column>
      <Button href="https://example.com" text="Open it" />
    </Column>
  </Row>
</Email>
```

```tsx
// After
<Email width={500} style={{ color: "#000000", fontFamily: "arial,helvetica,sans-serif" }}>
  <Section style={{ backgroundColor: "#ffffff" }}>
    <Row>
      <Column style={{ width: "50%" }}>
        <Heading style={{ padding: 10, fontSize: 22, fontWeight: 400, lineHeight: "140%" }}>
          Welcome, {name}
        </Heading>
        <Text style={{ padding: 10, fontSize: 14, lineHeight: "140%" }}>
          {"Your workspace is "}
          <Span style={{ fontWeight: 700 }}>ready</Span>.
        </Text>
      </Column>
      <Column style={{ width: "50%" }}>
        <Column style={{ padding: 10, alignItems: "center" }}>
          <Button href={{ href: "https://example.com", target: "_blank" }}>Open it</Button>
        </Column>
      </Column>
    </Row>
  </Section>
</Email>
```

The new design draws what the old template drew. Unlayer Elements' components filled in defaults (a 500px email, Arial, 10px of padding on every block), and the new ones don't, so the codemod writes those values out. Delete the ones you don't want.

## What it writes

| Older components | New elements |
|---|---|
| `Email`'s 500px, black text, Arial | `width={500}`, and the color and font in `style` |
| A block's 10px of padding (`containerPadding`) | `padding: 10` on the block, or on a `Column` around an `Image`, `Button`, `Social`, `Menu` or `Video` |
| `Heading`: 22px at 140%, not bold; `Paragraph`: 14px at 140% | Those values in `style` |
| `Paragraph` | `Text` |
| `headingType="h3"` | `level={3}` |
| `html="Hi <b>there</b>"` | Children: `Hi <Span style={{ fontWeight: 700 }}>there</Span>`. `<a>` becomes `Link` (its target and title kept), `<br>` `LineBreak`, `<s>`, `<sup>` and `<sub>` a `Span`. Entities are decoded. Each `<p>` is a blank line from the next, and another block starts a line of its own. |
| A text block's children, `text` and `html` | What the old one drew: a `Paragraph` its children, else its `text` (plain text), else its `html`; a `Heading` or a `Button` its `text` (as markup) over its children, never its `html` |
| `letterSpacing="0.05em"` | px, from the font size |
| A `Row` | A `Section` (its background across the window), with a `Row` of `Column`s for several columns, each its share of the layout as a `width` |
| A `Row`'s side padding | Dropped: the old one drew it outside the content, where it doesn't show |
| A line along the bottom (or top) of every `Column` of a `Row` | The `Row`'s border, and each `Column`'s on phones, where they stack |
| An `Image` 120px wide | The share of its column the old one drew it at (`width: "25%", maxWidth: 125` in a 500px email). Give it `width: 120` to draw it at 120px. |
| `html` with what a run of text can't hold (an image, a list, a table, a box in a line) | An `Html` block with that markup, in a `Column` with the text's styles |
| Markup a value decides or a list writes (`` `${note ? `<em>${note}</em>` : ""}` ``) | The same choice or list, of `Span`s and `Link`s |
| Lengths in rem, em, or following the window | px (rem and em at 16px; a width that follows the window at a phone's) |
| `Html` | `Html` in a `Column` with its padding |
| `Table`'s `headers` and `data`, or the `values` it can read | A `Table` of `TableRow`s and `TableCell`s |
| `Document`'s `documentSize`, `documentOrientation`, `documentMargin`; a `PageBreak` | `size`, `orientation`, `margin`; a `PageBreak` between `Section`s |
| `Button`'s `buttonColors` | Its `color` and `backgroundColor` in `style`, and its hover colors in `style={{ hover: { … } }}` |
| `mobile={{ ... }}`, `hideOnMobile`, `hideOnDesktop` | `style={{ mobile: { ... } }}` with the new names, `hidden={{ mobile: true }}` |
| `Social`'s `{ name, url }`; `Menu`'s `linkColor` and `textColor` | `{ name, href }`; `color` and `separatorColor` |

## What it notes

The codemod never drops anything quietly. It lists, with the line:

- a value it can't read from the source (an expression) where the old components drew something other than it says: an image's width, a `Row`'s padding, phone settings;
- `html` from an expression: it's written as text, so markup in it would show;
- markup the new elements don't write, each named (an image with its `src` and `alt`, a list's bullets, a style declaration and the tag it was on, a tag they have no run for), with the text in it kept;
- a text block's source the old one didn't draw (a `Paragraph`'s `html` beside its children);
- `Column`s whose borders or backgrounds the old components stretched to their `Row`'s height;
- a horizontal `Menu` of links written out, which becomes a wrapping `Row` of its links and separators so it draws the same (a `Menu` worked out at run time, or a vertical one, stays a `Menu`);
- custom tools, which it doesn't rewrite yet: a comment marks each one for you to rewrite;
- a `Table`'s or a text's values from code, written as text where the old ones drew them as HTML, so markup in them would show;
- old functions it leaves imported, such as `renderToHtml()`.

## What to check by hand

- **Rendering.** The new elements render with `await render(element)`, which is async, in place of `renderToHtml()`. Update every caller.
- **Notes.** Read every line of the report. Each one names a place where the output may differ or where you have work to do.
- **Custom tools.** Rewrite each one marked with a comment, with the new elements or `defineElement()`.
- **Values from expressions.** Image widths, `Row` padding and phone settings from code weren't read. Check them.
- **Markup in values.** `html` and table values from code are now text. If they held markup, rewrite them as `Span`s and `Link`s.
- **Runtime roots.** A template with `const Root = web ? Page : Email` wasn't changed. Write it with one root.
- **Look at it.** The codemod's tests check what each old component becomes, and round-trip each migrated example through the builder and back. No test draws a migrated template next to the old one in a browser, so render yours and look at it before you send it.

> **Tip:** Run `npx @hyper-elements/migrate src/emails --from unlayer-elements --report notes.md` first, without `--write`, and read `notes.md`. Then write.

---

# Elements reference

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements

Every element, what it holds, and every prop and style it takes, with its default and what it does. [Designs](https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/designs) shows how a design is written; `validate()` checks one against what's here.

Every element also takes:

- `style={{ … }}`: the styles listed under it. A number is px (`padding: 16` is `16px`).
- `style={{ mobile: { … } }}`: style overrides on phones, in an `Email` or a `Page`, for the styles listed under "`style.mobile`".
- `style={{ hover: { … } }}`: styles on hover, for the ones listed under "`style.hover`".
- `hidden={{ mobile: true }}` or `hidden={{ desktop: true }}`: shown on one only.
- `id`: an id of your own, written into the HTML.


A design is one of these, and the root decides the output: `render()` writes an Email's HTML, a Page's HTML, and a Document's print HTML. `renderPdf()` (`@hyper-elements/react/pdf`) writes a Document's PDF, and `renderImage()` (`@hyper-elements/react/image`) a Canvas's PNG or SVG (`render()` writes a Canvas's HTML, to look at).


Bands and boxes that arrange blocks. None is required: a root stacks its children.


Content, stacked down whatever holds it.


Inside text: a styled run, a link, a line break, a merge tag.


Only inside the element named: a list's items, a table's rows and cells, a document's pages, header and footer.


Only inside an Svg, in its viewBox's units.


`await render(design, { blockMap: true })` also gives `blocks`, for a tool that previews a design and needs to know which block of it it's looking at: `{ version, unit: "utf8", entries: [{ path, nodeId?, type, offset }] }`. Every root has one: an Email, a Page, a Document (its print HTML) and a Canvas (as HTML).

- Each block written as an element has an entry: its place in the design (`root.children[2]`, as diagnostics give it), its `id` where it has one, its element (`type`, as laid out: a Grid's rows are `Row`s), and the UTF-8 byte offset in `html` just after its outermost element's tag name (`<table`, `<div`). In an Email, that's the first element every email client but classic Outlook reads, else its first in Outlook's own markup.
- Entries are in the order of their offsets; at one offset, the outer block comes first. A `LineBreak`, a `MergeTag` and a `PageNumber` have none, nor, in an Email, a `Layer`'s `Image` (drawn as the Layer's background).
- A Document's `PageHeader` and `PageFooter`, and what they hold, are written on every page: they have an entry on each, with the same `path`. A `Document.Page`'s entry is its page's box.
- The HTML is the same bytes as without the option. Merge tags are written before the offsets are taken, and the offsets count the whole document, `<head>` included.
- `version` is `BLOCK_MAP_VERSION`, which changes only when this format does.
- Not with `pretty`, which indents the HTML after the offsets are taken (`render/block-map-pretty`).

## Values

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/values

What a property takes, where it says *kind*:

- *fontFaces*: a list of { family, src, format, weight, style }
- *color*: a color ("#0879a1", "rgb(…)", "rgba(…)" or a CSS name)
- *fontFamily*: a font stack, as CSS writes it ("Inter, Arial, sans-serif")
- *fontWeight*: 100 to 900 in hundreds, "normal" or "bold"
- *lineHeight*: a multiple of the font size (1.5), a percentage ("150%"), px ("24px") or "normal" (the font's own)
- *breakpoints*: { mobile }: the phone width in px (from 240)
- *insets*: px for all sides, "8px 16px" (1 to 4 values), [v, h] or [t, r, b, l], or { top, right, bottom, left }
- *border*: "1px solid #ccc", { width, style, color } for all sides, or { top, right, bottom, left } with one of those each
- *radius*: px for every corner, [topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft], or { topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft }
- *flex*: a share of the free width (0 or more), or "none"
- *link*: a URL (http, https, mailto, tel, a path, or a merge tag) or { href, target }
- *attributes*: attributes by name, each a text value (no on… handlers, href or style)
- *asset*: an image URL (http, https or a data:image URI), or { src, width, height }
- *line*: "1px solid #ccc" or { width, style, color }
- *video*: a YouTube or Vimeo video's https link

## Email

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/email

An email. Its children are stacked down the content width, centered in the window.

Holds: Section, Row, Column, Grid, Layer, Svg, Text, Heading, Link, Button, Image, Divider, List, Table, Video, Social, Menu, Html.

Props:
- `width`: a length (a number of px) (default `600`)
- `previewText`: text. Shown after the subject in inbox lists, not in the email.
- `title`: text. The document's title (shown in a browser tab, and by some email clients).
- `lang`: text. Its language, as a BCP 47 tag ("en", "ar").
- `dir`: one of "ltr", "rtl", "auto"
- `fonts`: *fontFaces*. The font files the design loads: a family's file for each weight and style it uses. Text names a family in its fontFamily stack, before the fonts to show where it can't load.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (default `"#000000"`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (default `"Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif"`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (default `16`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (default `400`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (default `1.5`, inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (default `"left"`, inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background). The window's background, behind the content.
- `gap`: a length (a number of px) (Spacing). Space between children.
- `alignItems`: one of "start", "center", "end", "stretch" (Layout). Where children sit across the layout's direction (vertically in a Row, horizontally in a Column), as CSS align-items. Across a Column it places what has its own size (a Button, an Image, an Svg, a box with a width); a block of text fills the width, so its words move with its textAlign.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textAlign`, `gap`.

## Page

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/page

A web page. Its children are stacked down the content width, centered in the window.

Holds: Section, Row, Column, Grid, Layer, Svg, Text, Heading, Link, Button, Image, Divider, List, Table, Video, Social, Menu, Html.

Props:
- `width`: a length (a number of px) (default `1200`). The widest the content gets.
- `description`: text. The page's meta description.
- `breakpoints`: *breakpoints*. Where its phone styles start: mobile, the widest window they apply to, in px (480 where it's not set).
- `title`: text. The document's title (shown in a browser tab, and by some email clients).
- `lang`: text. Its language, as a BCP 47 tag ("en", "ar").
- `dir`: one of "ltr", "rtl", "auto"
- `fonts`: *fontFaces*. The font files the design loads: a family's file for each weight and style it uses. Text names a family in its fontFamily stack, before the fonts to show where it can't load.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (default `"#000000"`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (default `"Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif"`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (default `16`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (default `400`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (default `1.5`, inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (default `"left"`, inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background). The window's background, behind the content.
- `gap`: a length (a number of px) (Spacing). Space between children.
- `alignItems`: one of "start", "center", "end", "stretch" (Layout). Where children sit across the layout's direction (vertically in a Row, horizontally in a Column), as CSS align-items. Across a Column it places what has its own size (a Button, an Image, an Svg, a box with a width); a block of text fills the width, so its words move with its textAlign.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `gap`.

## Document

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/document

A printed document: its children on pages of its size (Document.Page, or split by PageBreaks), a PageHeader and a PageFooter on each. Renders to print HTML, and to PDF with @hyper-elements/react/pdf.

Holds: Section, Row, Column, Grid, Layer, Svg, Text, Heading, Link, Button, Image, Divider, List, Table, Video, Social, Menu, Html, Document.Page, PageBreak, PageHeader, PageFooter.

Props:
- `size`: one of "A3", "A4", "A5", "Letter", "Legal", "Tabloid" (default `"A4"`)
- `orientation`: one of "portrait", "landscape" (default `"portrait"`)
- `margin`: *insets* (default `{"top":48,"right":48,"bottom":48,"left":48}`). Around each page's content (its header and footer too), in px: 96 to the inch.
- `title`: text. The document's title (shown in a browser tab, and by some email clients).
- `lang`: text. Its language, as a BCP 47 tag ("en", "ar").
- `dir`: one of "ltr", "rtl", "auto"
- `fonts`: *fontFaces*. The font files the design loads: a family's file for each weight and style it uses. Text names a family in its fontFamily stack, before the fonts to show where it can't load.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (default `"#000000"`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (default `"Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif"`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (default `16`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (default `400`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (default `1.5`, inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (default `"left"`, inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background). Each page's background, out to its edges.
- `gap`: a length (a number of px) (Spacing). Space between children.
- `alignItems`: one of "start", "center", "end", "stretch" (Layout). Where children sit across the layout's direction (vertically in a Row, horizontally in a Column), as CSS align-items. Across a Column it places what has its own size (a Button, an Image, an Svg, a box with a width); a block of text fills the width, so its words move with its textAlign.

## Canvas

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/canvas

An image of a fixed size (a social card, a banner): its children laid out in it as on a page. Written as PNG or SVG with @hyper-elements/react/image.

Holds: Section, Row, Column, Grid, Layer, Svg, Text, Heading, Link, Button, Image, Divider, List, Table, Video, Social, Menu, Html.

Props:
- `width`: a length (a number of px) (default `1200`). The image's width, in px.
- `height`: a length (a number of px) (default `630`). The image's height, in px: what's past it is cut.
- `title`: text. The document's title (shown in a browser tab, and by some email clients).
- `lang`: text. Its language, as a BCP 47 tag ("en", "ar").
- `dir`: one of "ltr", "rtl", "auto"
- `fonts`: *fontFaces*. The font files the design loads: a family's file for each weight and style it uses. Text names a family in its fontFamily stack, before the fonts to show where it can't load.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (default `"#000000"`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (default `"Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif"`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (default `16`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (default `400`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (default `1.5`, inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (default `"left"`, inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background). The window's background, behind the content.
- `gap`: a length (a number of px) (Spacing). Space between children.
- `alignItems`: one of "start", "center", "end", "stretch" (Layout). Where children sit across the layout's direction (vertically in a Row, horizontally in a Column), as CSS align-items. Across a Column it places what has its own size (a Button, an Image, an Svg, a box with a width); a block of text fills the width, so its words move with its textAlign.
- `padding`: *insets* (Spacing)
- `justifyContent`: one of "start", "center", "end", "space-between" (Layout). Where children sit along the layout's direction, as CSS justify-content.

## Section

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/section

A band across the whole window, directly in an Email or Page: its background spans the window, its children are stacked at the content width.

Holds: Row, Column, Grid, Layer, Svg, Text, Heading, Link, Button, Image, Divider, List, Table, Video, Social, Menu, Html.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background)
- `padding`: *insets* (Spacing)
- `border`: *border* (Border)
- `gap`: a length (a number of px) (Spacing). Space between children.
- `alignItems`: one of "start", "center", "end", "stretch" (Layout). Where children sit across the layout's direction (vertically in a Row, horizontally in a Column), as CSS align-items. Across a Column it places what has its own size (a Button, an Image, an Svg, a box with a width); a block of text fills the width, so its words move with its textAlign.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textAlign`, `padding`, `border`, `gap`.

## Row

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/row

Lays its children out side by side. A child takes its width, or a share of what's left (its flex, 1 by default).

Holds: Row, Column, Grid, Layer, Svg, Text, Heading, Link, Button, Image, Divider, List, Table, Video, Social, Menu, Html.

Props:
- `stackOnMobile`: true or false (default `true`). Its children stack full-width on phones (in an Email or a Page).
- `dir`: one of "ltr", "rtl", "auto". Its text's direction, where it differs from the design's; it starts on that side unless aligned otherwise.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `width`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `minWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `maxWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `height`: a length (a number of px) (Size)
- `padding`: *insets* (Spacing)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background)
- `border`: *border* (Border)
- `borderRadius`: *radius* (Border)
- `overflow`: one of "visible", "hidden" (Layout). Whether content past a set height is cut off.
- `gap`: a length (a number of px) (Spacing). Space between children.
- `alignItems`: one of "start", "center", "end", "stretch" (Layout). Where children sit across the layout's direction (vertically in a Row, horizontally in a Column), as CSS align-items. Across a Column it places what has its own size (a Button, an Image, an Svg, a box with a width); a block of text fills the width, so its words move with its textAlign.
- `justifyContent`: one of "start", "center", "end", "space-between" (Layout). Where children sit along the layout's direction, as CSS justify-content.
- `flexWrap`: one of "nowrap", "wrap", "words" (Layout). "wrap": children that don't fit wrap onto another line, as CSS flex-wrap (in an email, in a Row kept side by side on phones, with no gap between the lines). "words": in an email, also a space of the text's font apart, on lines at least as tall as its, as words are.
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textAlign`, `width`, `maxWidth`, `padding`, `border`, `gap`.

## Column

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/column

Stacks its children vertically, with its own spacing and box.

Holds: Row, Column, Grid, Layer, Svg, Text, Heading, Link, Button, Image, Divider, List, Table, Video, Social, Menu, Html.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `width`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `minWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `maxWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `height`: a length (a number of px) (Size)
- `padding`: *insets* (Spacing)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background)
- `border`: *border* (Border)
- `borderRadius`: *radius* (Border)
- `overflow`: one of "visible", "hidden" (Layout). Whether content past a set height is cut off.
- `gap`: a length (a number of px) (Spacing). Space between children.
- `alignItems`: one of "start", "center", "end", "stretch" (Layout). Where children sit across the layout's direction (vertically in a Row, horizontally in a Column), as CSS align-items. Across a Column it places what has its own size (a Button, an Image, an Svg, a box with a width); a block of text fills the width, so its words move with its textAlign.
- `justifyContent`: one of "start", "center", "end", "space-between" (Layout). Where children sit along the layout's direction, as CSS justify-content.
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textAlign`, `width`, `maxWidth`, `padding`, `border`, `gap`.

## Grid

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/grid

Its children in columns of equal width, row after row; on phones, one under another.

Holds: Row, Column, Grid, Layer, Svg, Text, Heading, Link, Button, Image, Divider, List, Table, Video, Social, Menu, Html.

Props:
- `columns`: an integer from 1 to 12 (default `2`). How many children to a row.
- `stackOnMobile`: true or false (default `true`). Its children one under another on phones (in an Email or a Page).

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `width`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `minWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `maxWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `height`: a length (a number of px) (Size)
- `padding`: *insets* (Spacing)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background)
- `border`: *border* (Border)
- `borderRadius`: *radius* (Border)
- `overflow`: one of "visible", "hidden" (Layout). Whether content past a set height is cut off.
- `gap`: a length (a number of px) (Spacing). Space between its children, across and down (unless rowGap is set).
- `rowGap`: a length (a number of px) (Spacing). Space between its rows (gap by default); on phones, where the children stack, gap is between them.
- `alignItems`: one of "start", "center", "end", "stretch" (Layout). Where each child sits in its row's height, as CSS align-items.
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textAlign`, `width`, `maxWidth`, `padding`, `border`, `gap`, `rowGap`.

## Layer

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/layer

Its children over each other, in one box as tall as the tallest: words on an image (a background image, its first child). In an email, an Image with one child over it.

Holds: Row, Column, Grid, Layer, Svg, Text, Heading, Link, Button, Image, Divider, List, Table, Video, Social, Menu, Html.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `width`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `minWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `maxWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background)
- `border`: *border* (Border)
- `borderRadius`: *radius* (Border)
- `height`: a length (a number of px) (Size). Its height: the image under its children covers it, cut at its sides or its top and bottom.
- `alignItems`: one of "start", "center", "end", "stretch" (default `"start"`, Layout). Where its children sit in its height, as CSS align-items.
- `justifyItems`: one of "start", "center", "end", "stretch" (default `"stretch"`, Layout). Where its children sit across its width, as CSS justify-items: stretched to it by default.
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textAlign`, `width`, `maxWidth`, `border`.

## Svg

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/svg

Shapes (Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Line, Polygon, Path) drawn in a box of its own: its width and height, and the coordinates its viewBox gives them.

Holds: Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Line, Polygon, Path. Not in an Email.

Props:
- `width`: a number from 0 (required)
- `height`: a number from 0 (required)
- `viewBox`: text. The shapes' coordinates in it, as "x y width height" (its width and height by default).
- `title`: text. What it shows, read out by screen readers.

`style`:
- `padding`: *insets* (Spacing)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background)
- `border`: *border* (Border)
- `borderRadius`: *radius* (Border)
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `padding`, `border`.

## Text

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/text

A paragraph of text.

Holds: text; PageNumber, Span, Link, LineBreak, MergeTag, Image.

Props:
- `dir`: one of "ltr", "rtl", "auto". Its text's direction, where it differs from the design's; it starts on that side unless aligned otherwise.
- `fit`: { sizes, maxLines } (only in Canvas). In a Canvas: sizes it may be drawn at (a list of px, or { min, max, step }), largest first, and the lines it may take (maxLines). The image draws the largest size that fits.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `textDecoration`: one of "none", "underline", "line-through" (Typography)
- `width`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `maxWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `padding`: *insets* (Spacing)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background)
- `border`: *border* (Border)
- `borderRadius`: *radius* (Border)
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textAlign`, `width`, `maxWidth`, `padding`, `border`.

## Heading

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/heading

A heading, from level 1 (the page's title) to 6.

Holds: text; PageNumber, Span, Link, LineBreak, MergeTag.

Props:
- `level`: one of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 (default `1`)
- `dir`: one of "ltr", "rtl", "auto". Its text's direction, where it differs from the design's; it starts on that side unless aligned otherwise.
- `fit`: { sizes, maxLines } (only in Canvas). In a Canvas: sizes it may be drawn at (a list of px, or { min, max, step }), largest first, and the lines it may take (maxLines). The image draws the largest size that fits.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (default `700`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (default `1.25`, inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `textDecoration`: one of "none", "underline", "line-through" (Typography)
- `width`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `maxWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `padding`: *insets* (Spacing)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background)
- `border`: *border* (Border)
- `borderRadius`: *radius* (Border)
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textAlign`, `width`, `maxWidth`, `padding`, `border`.

## Button

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/button

A link drawn as a button.

Holds: text; Span, MergeTag, LineBreak.

Props:
- `href`: *link* (required)
- `title`: text. Shown as a tooltip by mail clients and browsers that show one.
- `aria-label`: text. What a screen reader says for it, where its text alone doesn't say enough ("Read more about pricing").
- `attrs`: *attributes*. More attributes for its link: a class, a `data-` attribute.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (default `"#ffffff"`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (default `14`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (default `1.2`, inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (default `"center"`, inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `textDecoration`: one of "none", "underline", "line-through" (Typography)
- `width`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `maxWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `padding`: *insets* (default `{"top":10,"right":20,"bottom":10,"left":20}`, Spacing)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (default `"#0879a1"`, Background)
- `border`: *border* (Border)
- `borderRadius`: *radius* (default `4`, Border)
- `boxSizing`: one of "border-box", "content-box" (Size). Whether its width holds its padding and border (border-box), or they go on top of it (content-box).
- `alignSelf`: one of "start", "center", "end" (Layout). Where it sits in its stack, whatever the stack's alignItems: on phones too, another place than on desktop.
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.hover`: `color`, `backgroundColor`.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textAlign`, `width`, `maxWidth`, `padding`, `border`, `alignSelf`.

## Image

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/image

An image in the content. Without a width it takes its own size, no wider than its parent.

Holds: nothing.

Props:
- `src`: *asset* (required)
- `alt`: text (default `""`). Read out by screen readers, and shown where images don't load.
- `title`: text. Shown as a tooltip by mail clients and browsers that show one.

`style`:
- `width`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `maxWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `height`: a length (a number of px) (Size)
- `border`: *border* (Border)
- `borderRadius`: *radius* (Border)
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.
- `alignSelf`: one of "start", "center", "end" (Layout). Where it sits in its stack on phones, where that's another place than on desktop.
- `verticalAlign`: one of "top", "middle" (Layout). Where it sits in a line of text it's in.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `width`, `maxWidth`, `border`, `alignSelf`.

## Divider

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/divider

A horizontal line.

Holds: nothing.

`style`:
- `borderTop`: *line* (default `{"width":1,"style":"solid","color":"#bbbbbb"}`, Border). The line, as CSS border-top: "1px solid #bbbbbb".
- `width`: a length (a number of px, %) (default `"100%"`, Size)
- `padding`: *insets* (Spacing)

`style.mobile` (on phones): `width`, `padding`.

## List

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/list

A bulleted or numbered list of ListItems. Its markers sit in a column of their own (indent) before the items.

Holds: ListItem.

Props:
- `type`: one of "bullet", "number" (default `"bullet"`)
- `start`: an integer from 0 (default `1`). The first item's number, in a numbered list.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `width`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `maxWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `padding`: *insets* (Spacing)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background)
- `border`: *border* (Border)
- `gap`: a length (a number of px) (Spacing). Space between items.
- `indent`: a length (a number of px) (default `24`, Spacing). The width of the markers' column, before the items.
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textAlign`, `width`, `maxWidth`, `padding`, `border`, `gap`.

## Table

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/table

A table of data: TableRows of TableCells. Columns take their cells' widths; the rest share what's left.

Holds: TableRow.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `width`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `maxWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background)
- `border`: *border* (Border)
- `cellPadding`: *insets* (Spacing). Every cell's padding, where the cell doesn't set its own.
- `rowBorder`: *line* (Border)
- `borderCollapse`: one of "separate", "collapse" (Border). Whether cells side by side draw a border each (separate) or share one (collapse).
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `textAlign`, `width`, `maxWidth`, `border`.

## Video

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/video

A YouTube or Vimeo video: its player on a page; in an email (which can't play one), its thumbnail, linked to it.

Holds: nothing.

Props:
- `src`: *video* (required). The video's YouTube or Vimeo link.
- `thumbnail`: *asset*. The image an email shows, linked to the video. A YouTube video's own where there's none; a Vimeo video's can't be found without the network.
- `title`: text (default `"Video"`). The player's title on a page, the thumbnail's alternate text in an email.

`style`:
- `width`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `maxWidth`: a length (a number of px, %) (Size)
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `width`, `maxWidth`.

## Social

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/social

Links to social profiles: a line of the networks' icons, each linked to its profile.

Holds: nothing.

Props:
- `icons`: a list of icons, each { name, href } (required). Each network by name ("Instagram", "LinkedIn") and the link to its profile.
- `iconType`: one of "circle", "rounded", "squared" (default `"circle"`)
- `size`: an integer from 1 (default `32`). Each icon's width and height, in px.

`style`:
- `gap`: a length (a number of px) (default `5`, Spacing). Space between children.
- `justifyContent`: one of "start", "center", "end" (default `"center"`, Layout). Where the icons sit across the line.
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `gap`.

## Menu

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/menu

A line of links (a site's sections, a footer's), onto more lines where they don't fit, with a separator between them on desktop; or links down a column.

Holds: nothing.

Props:
- `items`: a list of items, each { text, href } (required). Each link's text and where it goes.
- `separator`: text (default `""`). Between the links of a horizontal menu ("|", "·"), on desktop: phones show none.
- `layout`: one of "horizontal", "vertical" (default `"horizontal"`)

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (default `"#0068A5"`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (default `14`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (default `1.2`, inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `separatorColor`: *color* (default `"#444444"`, Border)
- `padding`: *insets* (default `{"top":5,"right":15,"bottom":5,"left":15}`, Spacing). Around each link: its sides are the space between them.
- `justifyContent`: one of "start", "center", "end" (default `"center"`, Layout). Where the links sit.
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`.

## Html

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/html

Markup written as it is, for what no element says (the builder's HTML block): in an email and on a page as given, nothing in it checked or escaped. A Document's PDF and a Canvas's image draw its plain text.

Holds: nothing.

Props:
- `html`: text (required). The markup, written as it is: only markup you trust. Or give it as JSX inside the block, which React writes.
- `text`: text. What it reads as in the plain-text version, and in a PDF or an image (its markup's words where there's none).

## PageNumber

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/pagenumber

In a Document's text: the number of the page it's on, or (total) how many pages there are.

Holds: nothing. Only in a Document.

Props:
- `total`: true or false (default `false`). How many pages the Document has, instead of this page's number.

## Span

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/span

Styled text inside text; raised or lowered (superscript, subscript) with verticalAlign.

Holds: text; PageNumber, Span, Link, LineBreak, MergeTag.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `textDecoration`: one of "none", "underline", "line-through" (Typography)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background)
- `verticalAlign`: one of "baseline", "super", "sub" (Layout). "super": superscript (®, a footnote mark); "sub": subscript; as CSS vertical-align.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `letterSpacing`.

## Link

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/link

A link: text inside text, or around an Image.

Holds: text; PageNumber, Span, Link, LineBreak, MergeTag, Image.

Props:
- `href`: *link* (required)
- `title`: text. Shown as a tooltip by mail clients and browsers that show one.
- `aria-label`: text. What a screen reader says for it, where its text alone doesn't say enough ("Read more about pricing").
- `attrs`: *attributes*. More attributes for it: a class, a `data-` attribute.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (default `"#0000ee"`, inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `textDecoration`: one of "none", "underline", "line-through" (default `"underline"`, Typography)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background)
- `flex`: *flex* (Layout). In a Row: its share of the width left after children with a width (default 1); "none" takes its own size.

`style.hover`: `color`, `textDecoration`, `backgroundColor`.

`style.mobile` (on phones): `fontSize`, `letterSpacing`.

## LineBreak

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/linebreak

Starts a new line inside text.

Holds: nothing.

## MergeTag

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/mergetag

A value the sending service fills in (a name, a link), written in the service's own syntax.

Holds: nothing.

Props:
- `name`: text (required)

## Document.Page

Source: https://www.hyperelements.dev/docs/elements/document-page

One page of a Document (Document.Page in JSX): its children stacked down it, inside the Document's margins.

Holds: Section, Row, Column, Grid, Layer, Svg, Text, Heading, Link, Button, Image, Divider, List, Table, Video, Social, Menu, Html. Only in a Document.

`style`:
- `color`: *color* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontFamily`: *fontFamily* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontSize`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `fontWeight`: *fontWeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `fontStyle`: one of "normal", "italic" (inherited, Typography)
- `lineHeight`: *lineHeight* (inherited, Typography)
- `letterSpacing`: a length (a number of px) (inherited, Typography)
- `textAlign`: one of "left", "center", "right", "justify" (inherited, Typography)
- `textTransform`: one of "none", "uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize" (inherited, Typography)
- `backgroundColor`: *color* (Background). The page's background, out to its edges.
- `gap`: a length (a number of px) (Spacing). Space between children.
- `alignItems`: one of "start", "center", "end", "stretch" (Layout). Where children sit across the layout's direction (vertically in a Row, horizontally in a Column), as CSS align-items.
